```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. CLEAN HTML TABLE FUNCTION
# --------------------------------------------------

clean_table <- function(x, caption = NULL, digits = 2) {
  
  kableExtra::kbl(
    x,
    format = "html",
    caption = caption,
    digits = digits,
    escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      bootstrap_options = c(
        "striped",
        "hover",
        "condensed",
        "bordered"
      ),
      full_width = FALSE,
      position = "left"
    )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. HTML COLOUR SWATCH FUNCTION
# --------------------------------------------------

colour_swatch <- function(hex) {
  
  paste0(
    "<span style='display:inline-block;",
    "width:24px;height:15px;",
    "background-color:", hex, ";",
    "border:1px solid #555;",
    "vertical-align:middle;margin-right:8px;'></span>",
    
    "<code style='color:", hex, ";font-weight:bold;'>",
    hex,
    "</code>"
  )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. GGPlotly INTERACTIVITY FUNCTION
# --------------------------------------------------

interactive_plot <- function(p) {
  
  plotly::ggplotly(
    p,
    tooltip = "text",
    dynamicTicks = TRUE
  ) %>%
    
    plotly::config(
      displaylogo = FALSE,
      responsive = TRUE
    )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. SAMPLE POINTS FOR FASTER INTERACTIVE PLOTS
# --------------------------------------------------

# Sampling is ONLY for displaying points.
# Statistical models are fitted using the full datasets.

sample_by_groups <- function(data, group_vars, max_n = 2500) {
  
  data %>%
    
    group_by(
      across(all_of(group_vars))
    ) %>%
    
    group_modify(
      ~ {
        if (nrow(.x) > max_n) {
          dplyr::slice_sample(.x, n = max_n)
        } else {
          .x
        }
      }
    ) %>%
    
    ungroup()
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. REGRESSION LINE PREDICTION FUNCTION
# --------------------------------------------------

# Fits a linear model using ALL observations supplied.
# Returns only the predicted coordinates for plotting.

make_lm_line <- function(
    dat,
    yvar = "rating",
    label = "All films",
    x_limit = 300
) {
  
  dat <- dat %>%
    
    filter(
      !is.na(length),
      is.finite(.data[[yvar]])
    )
  
  if (
    nrow(dat) < 3 ||
    n_distinct(dat$length) < 2
  ) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  model_formula <- reformulate(
    "length",
    response = yvar
  )
  
  fit <- lm(
    model_formula,
    data = dat
  )
  
  xmin <- max(
    0,
    min(dat$length, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
  xmax <- min(
    x_limit,
    max(dat$length, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
  if (xmax <= xmin) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  x_values <- seq(
    xmin,
    xmax,
    length.out = 200
  )
  
  predictions <- predict(
    fit,
    newdata = tibble(length = x_values)
  )
  
  tibble(
    length = x_values,
    predicted = as.numeric(predictions),
    line_group = label
  )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. REGRESSION EQUATION SUMMARY FUNCTION
# --------------------------------------------------

linear_summary <- function(dat, label) {
  
  dat <- dat %>%
    
    filter(
      !is.na(length),
      !is.na(rating)
    )
  
  if (
    nrow(dat) < 3 ||
    n_distinct(dat$length) < 2
  ) {
    
    return(
      tibble(
        Group = label,
        N = nrow(dat),
        Equation = NA_character_,
        R_squared = NA_real_,
        Slope_p_value = NA_real_
      )
    )
  }
  
  fit <- lm(
    rating ~ length,
    data = dat
  )
  
  b <- coef(fit)
  
  p <- coef(summary(fit))[
    "length",
    "Pr(>|t|)"
  ]
  
  tibble(
    Group = label,
    
    N = nrow(dat),
    
    Equation = paste0(
      "rating = ",
      round(b[1], 4),
      
      ifelse(
        b[2] >= 0,
        " + ",
        " - "
      ),
      
      round(abs(b[2]), 5),
      " x length"
    ),
    
    R_squared = summary(fit)$r.squared,
    
    Slope_p_value = p
  )
}
```

# 1. Research objectives

The principal objective of this analysis is to investigate the relationship between movie duration and audience ratings.

The main research question is:
  
  **Does movie duration relate to audience ratings, and how does this relationship differ across film classifications, genres and historical periods?**
  
  Additional questions investigate:
  
  1. How movie duration is distributed across short films and other films.
2. Whether movie duration has changed over time.
3. Whether duration relates to audience engagement.
4. Whether viewers agree or disagree about the quality of movies.
5. How accurately the distribution of individual ratings approximates the actual average rating.
6. Whether budget and MPAA metadata availability is associated with movie characteristics and ratings.

All movie durations are represented by the original `length` variable, measured in minutes.

`Short` is treated as an independent film classification, not as a duration threshold and not as one of the six content genres.

# 2. Dataset preparation

## 2.1 Load the dataset

```{r load-data}

data("movies", package = "ggplot2movies")

movies_raw <- as_tibble(movies) %>%
  
  mutate(
    movie_id = row_number()
  )

dim(movies_raw)

head(movies_raw)

```

The dataset contains `r nrow(movies_raw)` movies and `r ncol(movies_raw) - 1` original variables.

## 2.2 Film classification colours

Other films are represented using bright orange.

Short films are represented using contrasting blue.

```{r film-colours}

film_fill <- c(
  "Other film" = "#E69F00",
  "Short film" = "#0072B2"
)

film_colour_key <- tibble(
  
  Film_classification = names(film_fill),
  
  Colour = map_chr(
    unname(film_fill),
    colour_swatch
  )
)

clean_table(
  film_colour_key,
  "Film classification colour scheme"
)

```

## 2.3 Genre colour alchemy

The six content genres are assigned individual base colours.

`Short` is deliberately excluded because it represents film classification.

```{r genre-colours}

genres <- c(
  "Action",
  "Animation",
  "Comedy",
  "Documentary",
  "Drama",
  "Romance"
)

genre_palette <- c(
  Action      = "#E41A1C",
  Animation   = "#377EB8",
  Comedy      = "#4DAF4A",
  Documentary = "#111111",
  Drama       = "#FF7F00",
  Romance     = "#984EA3"
)

genre_colour_key <- tibble(
  
  Genre = names(genre_palette),
  
  Colour = map_chr(
    unname(genre_palette),
    colour_swatch
  )
)

clean_table(
  genre_colour_key,
  "Individual genre colours"
)

```

Each movie's border colour is calculated by mixing the RGB components of all the genres to which it belongs.

For example:

- Action + Animation creates a mixture of red and blue.
- Comedy + Drama creates a mixture of green and orange.
- Action + Animation + Documentary creates a darker mixed colour.

This is a visual encoding, not a measure of biological or semantic similarity between genres.

```{r colour-mixing-function}

mix_genre_colours <- function(x) {

  active <- names(genre_palette)[

    !is.na(x[names(genre_palette)]) &

      x[names(genre_palette)] == 1
  ]

  if (length(active) == 0) {
    return("#808080")
  }

  # Extract RGB values of all applicable genres

  rgb_values <- grDevices::col2rgb(
    genre_palette[active]
  )

  # Calculate average RGB components

  mixed <- rowMeans(rgb_values)

  # Produce composite hexadecimal colour

  grDevices::rgb(
    red = mixed[1],
    green = mixed[2],
    blue = mixed[3],
    maxColorValue = 255
  )
}

# Identify the combination of genres

get_genre_combination <- function(x) {

  active <- names(genre_palette)[

    !is.na(x[names(genre_palette)]) &

      x[names(genre_palette)] == 1
  ]

  if (length(active) == 0) {
    return("No listed genre")
  }

  paste(
    active,
    collapse = " + "
  )
}

```

## 2.4 Construct the analytical dataset

```{r prepare-dataset}

genre_matrix <- as.matrix(
  movies_raw[, genres]
)

movies_analysis <- movies_raw %>%

  mutate(

    # Clean MPAA classification

    mpaa_clean = na_if(
      trimws(as.character(mpaa)),
      ""
    ),

    # Independent film classification

    film_type = case_when(
      Short == 1 ~ "Short film",
      Short == 0 ~ "Other film",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    film_type = factor(
      film_type,
      levels = c(
        "Other film",
        "Short film"
      )
    ),

    # Budget availability

    has_budget = !is.na(budget),

    # MPAA availability

    has_mpaa = !is.na(mpaa_clean),

    # Four mutually exclusive combinations

    metadata_group = case_when(

      has_budget & has_mpaa ~ "Both recorded",

      has_budget & !has_mpaa ~ "Budget only",

      !has_budget & has_mpaa ~ "MPAA only",

      !has_budget & !has_mpaa ~ "Neither recorded"
    ),

    metadata_group = factor(
      metadata_group,

      levels = c(
        "Neither recorded",
        "Budget only",
        "MPAA only",
        "Both recorded"
      )
    ),

    release_decade = floor(year / 10) * 10
  )

# Calculate genre combination for every movie

movies_analysis$genre_combination <- apply(
  genre_matrix,
  1,
  get_genre_combination
)

# Calculate the mixed border colour for every movie

movies_analysis$genre_border <- apply(
  genre_matrix,
  1,
  mix_genre_colours
)

# Interior fill

movies_analysis$point_fill <- unname(
  film_fill[
    as.character(movies_analysis$film_type)
  ]
)

# HTML hover information

movies_analysis$hover_text <- paste0(

  "<b>",
  htmltools::htmlEscape(
    movies_analysis$title
  ),
  "</b>",

  "<br>Year: ",
  movies_analysis$year,

  "<br>Duration: ",
  movies_analysis$length,
  " minutes",

  "<br>Rating: ",
  movies_analysis$rating,

  "<br>Votes: ",
  comma(movies_analysis$votes),

  "<br>Film type: ",
  movies_analysis$film_type,

  "<br>Genres: ",
  movies_analysis$genre_combination,

  "<br>Budget: ",
  comma(movies_analysis$budget),

  "<br>MPAA: ",
  movies_analysis$mpaa_clean
)

dim(movies_analysis)

```

## 2.5 Genre combination legend

This table displays the actual genre combinations present in the dataset and their calculated colours.

```{r genre-combination-legend}

genre_combinations <- movies_analysis %>%

  count(

    genre_border,
    name = "Number_of_movies"
  ) %>%

  arrange(
    desc(Number_of_movies)
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    Mixed_colour = map_chr(
      genre_border,

  select(
    Genre_combination = genre_combination,
    Mixed_colour,
    Number_of_movies

clean_table(

```

Every observed combination is listed separately, even when two different combinations happen to produce the same RGB mixture.

# 3. Initial data exploration

## 3.1 Missing-value overview

The missing-value overview is restricted to the two variables with missing information: `budget` and cleaned `mpaa_clean`.

```{r missing-values}

missing_summary <- tibble(

  Variable = c(
    "budget",
    "mpaa_clean"
  ),

  Missing_values = c(
    sum(is.na(movies_analysis$budget)),
    sum(is.na(movies_analysis$mpaa_clean))
  )

) %>%

  mutate(
    Missing_percentage =
      100 * Missing_values / nrow(movies_analysis)
  )

clean_table(
  missing_summary,
  "Missing-value overview"
)

```

Blank MPAA strings are treated as missing values.

A recorded budget of zero remains a recorded value.

## 3.2 Numerical descriptive statistics

The following table summarises the principal numerical variables without generating repetitive separate tables.

```{r numerical-statistics}

numeric_variables <- c(
  "year",
  "length",
  "budget",
  "rating",
  "votes"
)

numerical_summary <- map_dfr(

  numeric_variables,

  function(variable) {

    x <- movies_analysis[[variable]]

    x <- x[!is.na(x)]

    tibble(

      Variable = variable,

      N = length(x),

      Mean = mean(x),

      SD = sd(x),

      Median = median(x),

      Q1 = unname(

      ),

      Q3 = unname(
        quantile(x, 0.75)

      Maximum = max(x)

)

clean_table(

  "Descriptive statistics of principal numerical variables",
  digits = 2
)

```

## 3.3 Genre frequency pie chart

The percentages represent the share of all genre assignments, not the share of unique movies, because a movie may belong to several genres.

```{r genre-frequency}

genre_frequency <- map_dfr(

  genres,

  function(g) {

    tibble(
      Genre = g,
      Count = sum(
        movies_analysis[[g]] == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    )
  }

) %>%

  mutate(

    Percentage = Count / sum(Count),

    Percentage_label = scales::percent(
      Percentage,
      accuracy = 0.1
    ),

    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", Genre, "</b>",
      "<br>Number of movies: ",
      scales::comma(Count),
      "<br>Share of genre assignments: ",
      scales::percent(Percentage, accuracy = 0.1)
    )
  )

# Construct using ggplot2

genre_pie <- ggplot(
  genre_frequency,

  aes(
    x = "",
    y = Count,
    fill = Genre
  )
) +

  ggiraph::geom_col_interactive(

    aes(
      tooltip = hover_text,
      data_id = Genre
    ),

    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 1,
    width = 1
  ) +

  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = Percentage_label
    ),

    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),

    colour = "white",

    size = 3.5,

    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = genre_palette
  ) +

  coord_polar(
    theta = "y"
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Movie Genre Assignments",

    subtitle = "A movie may belong to multiple genres",

    fill = "Genre"
  ) +

  theme_void() +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 15
    ),

    legend.position = "right"
  )

# Interactive HTML output

ggiraph::girafe(

  ggobj = genre_pie,

  width_svg = 9,

  options = list(

    ggiraph::opts_hover(
```

# 4. Movie duration and film classification

## 4.1 Prepare the runtime dataset

The runtime visualisations display movies between 0 and 300 minutes.

Extreme durations remain in the original dataset and are investigated separately.

```{r runtime-data}

movies_display <- movies_analysis %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(length),
    length >= 0,
    length <= 300
  )

runtime_summary <- movies_display %>%

  group_by(film_type) %>%

  summarise(

    N = n(),

    Mean = mean(length),

    Median = median(length),

    Q1 = quantile(length, 0.25),

    Q3 = quantile(length, 0.75),

    SD = sd(length),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

clean_table(
  runtime_summary,
  "Runtime statistics by film classification"
)

```

## 4.2 Distribution of movie durations

Ten-minute duration intervals are used.

The graph displays separate panels but maintains the same X-axis scale.

```{r runtime-histogram}

runtime_bins <- movies_display %>%

  mutate(

    bin_start = floor(length / 10) * 10,

    bin_mid = bin_start + 5
  ) %>%

  count(
    film_type,
    bin_start,
    bin_mid
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", film_type, "</b>",
      "<br>Duration: ",
      bin_start, "–", bin_start + 10,
      " minutes",
      "<br>Number of movies: ",
      comma(n)
    )
  )

runtime_hist <- ggplot(
  runtime_bins,

  aes(
    x = bin_mid,
    y = n,
    fill = film_type
  )
) +

  geom_col(
    aes(text = hover_text),

    width = 9.5,

    colour = "white",

    linewidth = 0.4,

    alpha = 0.9
  ) +

  geom_vline(
    data = runtime_summary,

    aes(
      xintercept = Median
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = "black",

    linetype = "dashed",

    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~film_type,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = film_fill
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 300, 15),
    limits = c(0, 300),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,
    breaks = pretty_breaks(n = 6)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Movie Durations",

    subtitle = paste(
      "Ten-minute bins;",
      "dashed vertical line represents median duration"
    ),

    x = "Movie duration (minutes)",

    y = "Number of movies",

    fill = "Film classification"
  ) +

  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8),

    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "grey75",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.5
    )
  )

interactive_plot(runtime_hist)

```

# 5. Main relationship: Movie duration vs audience rating

## 5.1 Complete interactive scatterplot

This is the main scatterplot.

Unlike the secondary regression visualisations, this plot retains **all available movies with runtime up to 300 minutes**.

It uses Plotly WebGL for fast rendering of the full dataset.

The main analytical work still uses ggplot2 throughout the other figures.


```{r main-scatterplot}

# =========================================================
# 1. PREPARE THE DATA
# =========================================================

genre_columns <- c(
  "Action", "Animation", "Comedy",
  "Documentary", "Drama", "Romance"
)

main_scatter_data <- movies_display %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(length),
    !is.na(rating)
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    film_type = as.character(film_type),

    # Interior colour according to film classification
    film_colour = unname(film_fill[film_type]),

    # Budget
    budget_display = ifelse(
      is.na(budget),
      "Not recorded",
      scales::dollar(budget, accuracy = 1)
    ),

    # MPAA
    mpaa_display = ifelse(
      is.na(mpaa) | trimws(as.character(mpaa)) == "",
      "Not recorded",
      as.character(mpaa)
    ),

    # Votes
    votes_display = ifelse(
      is.na(votes),
      "Not recorded",
      scales::comma(votes)
    ),

    # Ensure every movie has a genre-border colour
    genre_border = ifelse(
      is.na(genre_border),
      "#808080",
      genre_border
    )
  )


# =========================================================
# 2. CREATE GENRE COMBINATIONS
# =========================================================

genre_matrix <- as.matrix(
  main_scatter_data[, genre_columns, drop = FALSE]
)

main_scatter_data$genre_combo <- apply(

  genre_matrix,

  1,

  function(z) {

    active_genres <- genre_columns[
      !is.na(z) & z == 1
    ]

    if (length(active_genres) == 0) {
      return("No recorded genre")
    }

    paste(
      active_genres,
      collapse = " + "
    )

  }
)


# =========================================================
# 3. GROUP MOVIES SHARING THE SAME COORDINATES
#
# Every movie with an identical runtime and rating
# is placed in the same coordinate group.
#
# The grouped information is stored as JSON.
# =========================================================

hover_groups <- main_scatter_data %>%

  group_by(length, rating) %>%

  group_modify(~ {

    dat <- .x

    group_info <- .y

    movie_cards <- lapply(

      seq_len(nrow(dat)),

      function(i) {

        list(

          title = as.character(dat$title[i]),

          year = ifelse(
            is.na(dat$year[i]),
            "Unknown",
            as.character(dat$year[i])
          ),

          length = group_info$length[[1]],

          rating = group_info$rating[[1]],

          votes = dat$votes_display[i],

          film_type = dat$film_type[i],

          film_colour = dat$film_colour[i],

          genre = dat$genre_combo[i],

          genre_border = dat$genre_border[i],

          budget = dat$budget_display[i],

          mpaa = dat$mpaa_display[i]

        )

      }
    )

    tibble::tibble(

      group_payload = as.character(

        jsonlite::toJSON(
          movie_cards,
          auto_unbox = TRUE,
          na = "null"
        )

      )

    )

  }) %>%

  ungroup()


# =========================================================
# 4. ATTACH GROUPED INFORMATION TO EVERY MOVIE
# =========================================================

main_scatter_data <- main_scatter_data %>%

  left_join(
    hover_groups,
    by = c("length", "rating")
  )


# =========================================================
# 5. BUILD THE SCATTERPLOT
# =========================================================

main_scatter <- plotly::plot_ly() %>%


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # OTHER FILMS: ORANGE INTERIOR
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(

    data = filter(
      main_scatter_data,
      film_type == "Other film"
    ),

    x = ~length,

    y = ~rating,

    customdata = ~group_payload,

    type = "scattergl",

    mode = "markers",

    marker = list(

      color = film_fill[["Other film"]],

      size = 6,

      opacity = 0.8,

      line = list(
        color = ~genre_border,
        width = 1.3
      )

    ),

    # Disable default Plotly tooltip but retain hover events
    hoverinfo = "none",

    name = "Other film"

  ) %>%


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # SHORT FILMS: BLUE INTERIOR
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  add_trace(

    data = filter(
      main_scatter_data,
      film_type == "Short film"
    ),

    x = ~length,

    y = ~rating,

    customdata = ~group_payload,

    type = "scattergl",

    mode = "markers",

    marker = list(

      color = film_fill[["Short film"]],

      size = 6,

      opacity = 0.8,

      line = list(
        color = ~genre_border,
        width = 1.3
      )

    ),

    hoverinfo = "none",

    name = "Short film"

  ) %>%


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # PLOT LAYOUT
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  layout(

    title = list(
      text = "Movie Duration vs Average IMDb Rating",
      x = 0.02
    ),

    xaxis = list(
      title = "Movie duration (minutes)",
      range = c(0, 300),
      dtick = 15,
      gridcolor = "#E5E5E5"
    ),

    yaxis = list(
      title = "Average IMDb rating",
      range = c(1, 10),
      dtick = 1,
      gridcolor = "#E5E5E5"
    ),

    hovermode = "closest",

    legend = list(
      title = list(
        text = "Film classification"
      )
    )

  ) %>%

  config(
    displaylogo = FALSE,
    responsive = TRUE
  )


# =========================================================
# 6. ROTATING MOVIE SELECTOR
#
# Initial delay:  2000 milliseconds
# Movie duration: 3000 milliseconds
# =========================================================

main_scatter <- htmlwidgets::onRender(

  main_scatter,

  r"(
  function(el, x) {

    const gd = el;


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // A. CREATE THE OVERLAY
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    gd.style.position = "relative";

    const overlay = document.createElement("div");

    overlay.style.cssText = `
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      width: 100%;
      height: 100%;
      z-index: 50;
      pointer-events: none;
      overflow: hidden;
    `;


    // SVG for connecting wires and central hub

    const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

    const svg = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "svg"
    );

    svg.style.cssText = `
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      width: 100%;
      height: 100%;
    `;


    // HTML layer for movie cards

    const cardLayer = document.createElement("div");

    cardLayer.style.cssText = `
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      width: 100%;
      height: 100%;
    `;


    overlay.appendChild(svg);

    overlay.appendChild(cardLayer);

    gd.appendChild(overlay);


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // B. ANIMATION STATE
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    let rotationTimer = null;

    let startTimer = null;

    let unhoverTimer = null;

    let activeKey = null;

    let currentIndex = 0;

    let activeMovies = [];

    let activeAnchor = null;


    // Stop the carousel interval

    function stopRotation() {

      if (rotationTimer !== null) {

        clearInterval(rotationTimer);

        rotationTimer = null;

      }

    }


    // Completely clear the selector and all timers

    function clearDisplay() {

      stopRotation();

      if (startTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(startTimer);

        startTimer = null;

      }

      if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

        unhoverTimer = null;

      }

      svg.innerHTML = "";

      cardLayer.innerHTML = "";

      activeKey = null;

      activeMovies = [];

      activeAnchor = null;

      currentIndex = 0;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // C. HELPER FUNCTIONS
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function clamp(value, min, max) {

      return Math.min(
        Math.max(value, min),
        max
      );

    }


    function addText(parent, tag, value, css) {

      const node = document.createElement(tag);

      node.textContent =
        value === null || value === undefined
          ? "Not recorded"
          : String(value);

      if (css) {

        node.style.cssText = css;

      }

      parent.appendChild(node);

      return node;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // D. DRAW CONNECTING WIRE
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function drawWire(

      anchorX,
      anchorY,
      cardX,
      cardY,
      colour,
      cardWidth,
      cardHeight

    ) {

      const dx = cardX - anchorX;

      const dy = cardY - anchorY;

      const distance = Math.sqrt(
        dx * dx + dy * dy
      );

      if (distance < 1) return;


      const ux = dx / distance;

      const uy = dy / distance;


      // Start outside central hub

      const startX = anchorX + ux * 18;

      const startY = anchorY + uy * 18;


      // End at nearest card boundary

      const factor = 1 / Math.max(

        Math.abs(dx) / (cardWidth / 2),

        Math.abs(dy) / (cardHeight / 2)

      );


      const endX = cardX - dx * factor;

      const endY = cardY - dy * factor;


      const line = document.createElementNS(
        svgNS,
        "line"
      );

      line.setAttribute("x1", startX);

      line.setAttribute("y1", startY);

      line.setAttribute("x2", endX);

      line.setAttribute("y2", endY);

      line.setAttribute("stroke", colour);

      line.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2.5");

      line.setAttribute("stroke-opacity", "0.85");

      svg.appendChild(line);

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // E. DRAW CENTRAL HUB
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function drawHub(anchorX, anchorY, total) {

      const circle = document.createElementNS(
        svgNS,
        "circle"
      );

      circle.setAttribute("cx", anchorX);

      circle.setAttribute("cy", anchorY);

      circle.setAttribute("r", "18");

      circle.setAttribute("fill", "#263238");

      circle.setAttribute("stroke", "#FFFFFF");

      circle.setAttribute("stroke-width", "3");

      svg.appendChild(circle);


      const number = document.createElementNS(
        svgNS,
        "text"
      );

      number.setAttribute("x", anchorX);

      number.setAttribute("y", anchorY + 4);

      number.setAttribute("text-anchor", "middle");

      number.setAttribute("font-size", "11");

      number.setAttribute("font-weight", "bold");

      number.setAttribute("fill", "#FFFFFF");

      number.textContent = total;

      svg.appendChild(number);

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // F. CREATE INDIVIDUAL MOVIE CARD
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function createMovieCard(movie, index, total) {

      const filmColour =
        movie.film_colour || "#777777";

      const genreColour =
        movie.genre_border || "#AAAAAA";


      // Serial number

      const serial = String(index + 1).padStart(2, "0");

      const totalSerial = String(total).padStart(2, "0");


      const card = document.createElement("div");

      card.style.cssText = `
        position: absolute;
        width: 260px;
        min-height: 160px;
        box-sizing: border-box;
        padding: 13px;
        background: rgba(255,255,255,0.98);
        border: 2px solid ${filmColour};
        border-left: 7px solid ${genreColour};
        border-radius: 12px;
        box-shadow: 0 6px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.23);
        color: #263238;
        font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
        line-height: 1.4;
        transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
        animation: movieCardAppear 0.25s ease-out;
      `;


      // Card header

      const header = document.createElement("div");

      header.style.cssText = `
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: space-between;
        margin-bottom: 9px;
      `;


      // Serial number

      addText(

        header,

        "span",

        `MOVIE ${serial} / ${totalSerial}`,

        `
          font-size: 13px;
          font-weight: bold;
          color: ${filmColour};
          letter-spacing: 0.5px;
        `

      );


      // Film classification

      addText(

        header,

        "span",

        movie.film_type,

        `
          font-size: 10px;
          font-weight: bold;
          color: ${filmColour};
          border: 1px solid ${filmColour};
          border-radius: 12px;
          padding: 3px 7px;
        `

      );


      card.appendChild(header);


      // Movie title

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `${movie.title} (${movie.year})`,

        `
          font-size: 15px;
          font-weight: bold;
          color: #17202A;
          margin-bottom: 7px;
        `

      );


      // Runtime, rating and votes

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `${movie.length} min  ·  Rating ${movie.rating}  ·  Votes ${movie.votes}`,

        `
          font-size: 11px;
          margin-bottom: 6px;
        `

      );


      // Genre combination

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `Genres: ${movie.genre}`,

        `
          font-size: 11px;
          margin-bottom: 6px;
          color: #46545F;
        `

      );


      // Budget

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `Budget: ${movie.budget}`,

        `
          font-size: 10px;
          color: #64717B;
        `

      );


      // MPAA

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `MPAA: ${movie.mpaa}`,

        `
          font-size: 10px;
          color: #64717B;
        `

      );


      cardLayer.appendChild(card);

      return card;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // G. DISPLAY ONE MOVIE
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function renderMovie(index) {

      if (!activeMovies.length || !activeAnchor) {

        return;

      }


      const total = activeMovies.length;

      const movie = activeMovies[index];

      const anchorX = activeAnchor.x;

      const anchorY = activeAnchor.y;

      const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


      // Remove previous card and wire

      svg.innerHTML = "";

      cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


      // Card dimensions and circular arrangement

      const cardWidth = 260;

      const cardHeight = 160;

      const radius = 185;


      // Start at top and move clockwise

      const angle =
        -Math.PI / 2 +
        (2 * Math.PI * index / total);


      let cardX =
        anchorX + radius * Math.cos(angle);

      let cardY =
        anchorY + radius * Math.sin(angle);


      // Keep card within plotting area

      const leftBound =
        size.l + cardWidth / 2 + 5;

      const rightBound =
        size.l + size.w - cardWidth / 2 - 5;

      const topBound =
        size.t + cardHeight / 2 + 5;

      const bottomBound =
        size.t + size.h - cardHeight / 2 - 5;


      cardX = clamp(
        cardX,
        leftBound,
        rightBound
      );

      cardY = clamp(
        cardY,
        topBound,
        bottomBound
      );


      // Connecting wire

      drawWire(

        anchorX,
        anchorY,

        cardX,
        cardY,

        movie.film_colour || "#777777",

        cardWidth,
        cardHeight

      );


      // Central hub

      drawHub(
        anchorX,
        anchorY,
        total
      );


      // Selected movie card

      const card = createMovieCard(
        movie,
        index,
        total
      );

      card.style.left = `${cardX}px`;

      card.style.top = `${cardY}px`;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // H. HANDLE HOVER EVENTS
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    gd.on("plotly_hover", function(eventData) {

      if (
        !eventData ||
        !eventData.points ||
        eventData.points.length === 0
      ) {

        return;

      }


      // Cancel pending unhover reset

      if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

        unhoverTimer = null;

      }


      const point = eventData.points[0];


      // Identify hovered coordinate

      const key = `${point.x}|${point.y}`;


      // Repeated events at the same point should
      // not restart the delay or carousel.

      if (key === activeKey) {

        return;

      }


      // Cancel all previous timers

      stopRotation();

      if (startTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(startTimer);

        startTimer = null;

      }


      svg.innerHTML = "";

      cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


      // -------------------------------------------------
      // READ GROUPED MOVIE INFORMATION
      // -------------------------------------------------

      let raw = point.customdata;


      // Handle array-wrapped customdata

      if (
        Array.isArray(raw) &&
        raw.length === 1 &&
        typeof raw[0] === "string"
      ) {

        raw = raw[0];

      }


      // Fallback to the trace customdata

      if (
        raw === undefined &&
        point.data &&
        point.data.customdata
      ) {

        raw = point.data.customdata[
          point.pointNumber
        ];

      }


      let movies;

      try {

        movies = typeof raw === "string"
          ? JSON.parse(raw)
          : raw;

      } catch (error) {

        console.error(
          "Could not read grouped movie information:",
          error
        );

        return;

      }


      if (!Array.isArray(movies)) {

        movies = [movies];

      }


      if (!movies.length) {

        return;

      }


      // -------------------------------------------------
      // STORE THE NEW SELECTION
      // -------------------------------------------------

      activeKey = key;

      activeMovies = movies;

      currentIndex = 0;


      // Convert data coordinates into pixel coordinates

      const xAxis = point.xaxis;

      const yAxis = point.yaxis;

      const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


      const anchorX =

        (xAxis._offset || size.l) +

        xAxis.d2p(point.x);


      const anchorY =

        (yAxis._offset || size.t) +

        yAxis.d2p(point.y);


      activeAnchor = {

        x: anchorX,

        y: anchorY

      };


      // -------------------------------------------------
      // 2-SECOND INITIAL DELAY
      // -------------------------------------------------

      // Nothing appears during the initial delay.
      // Movie 01 appears after two seconds.

      startTimer = setTimeout(function() {

        startTimer = null;


        // Ensure the cursor is still over this point

        if (
          activeKey !== key ||
          !activeMovies.length ||
          !activeAnchor
        ) {

          return;

        }


        // Display movie 01

        currentIndex = 0;

        renderMovie(0);


        // -------------------------------------------------
        // ROTATE EVERY 3 SECONDS
        // -------------------------------------------------

        // One movie = static card.
        // Multiple movies = one card every 3000 ms.

        if (activeMovies.length > 1) {

          rotationTimer = setInterval(function() {

            if (activeKey !== key) {

              stopRotation();

              return;

            }


            currentIndex =

              (currentIndex + 1) % activeMovies.length;


            renderMovie(currentIndex);

          }, 3000);

        }

      }, 2000);

    });


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // I. HANDLE UNHOVER
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    gd.on("plotly_unhover", function() {

      // Brief grace period avoids interruptions when
      // moving between overlapping traces.

      if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      }

      unhoverTimer = setTimeout(function() {

        clearDisplay();

      }, 80);

    });


    // Leaving the entire chart stops everything

    gd.addEventListener(
      "mouseleave",
      clearDisplay
    );


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // J. CARD APPEARANCE ANIMATION
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    const style = document.createElement("style");

    style.textContent = `

      @keyframes movieCardAppear {

        from {

          opacity: 0;

          transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scale(0.93);

        }

        to {

          opacity: 1;

          transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scale(1);

        }

      }

    `;

    document.head.appendChild(style);

  }
  )"
)


# =========================================================
# 7. DISPLAY THE FINAL SCATTERPLOT
# =========================================================

main_scatter

```

Hover over an individual movie to see its title, year, runtime, rating, vote count, film classification, genre combination, budget and MPAA classification.

# 6. Linear relationships and regression equations

Three models are calculated using the complete dataset:

1. All films.
2. Other films.
3. Short films.

The regression lines use:

- Red dashed: Other films.
- Blue dashed: Short films.
- Black solid: All films combined.


```{r linear-relationship}
# =========================================================
# 6.1 CALCULATE REGRESSION EQUATIONS
# =========================================================

linear_equations <- bind_rows(

  linear_summary(
    filter(
      main_scatter_data,
      film_type == "Other film"
    ),
    "Other films"
  ),

  linear_summary(
    filter(
      main_scatter_data,
      film_type == "Short film"
    ),
    "Short films"
  ),

  linear_summary(
    main_scatter_data,
    "All films"
  )
)

clean_table(
  linear_equations,
  "Regression equations fitted using all observations",
  digits = 5
)


# =========================================================
# 6.2 PRECOMPUTE REGRESSION LINES USING FULL DATASET
# =========================================================

line_data <- bind_rows(

  make_lm_line(
    filter(
      main_scatter_data,
      film_type == "Other film"
    ),
    yvar = "rating",
    label = "Other films"
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      line_colour = "#D62728",
      line_type = "dashed"
    ),

  make_lm_line(
    filter(
      main_scatter_data,
      film_type == "Short film"
    ),
    yvar = "rating",
    label = "Short films"
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      line_colour = "#0072B2",
      line_type = "dashed"
    ),

  make_lm_line(
    main_scatter_data,
    yvar = "rating",
    label = "All films"
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      line_colour = "black",
      line_type = "solid"
    )
)


# =========================================================
# 6.3 SAMPLE POINTS FOR DISPLAY
#
# Maximum 2500 per film classification.
# Regression calculations still use the complete dataset.
# =========================================================

set.seed(2026)

plot_sample <- sample_by_groups(
  main_scatter_data,
  group_vars = "film_type",
  max_n = 2500
)


# =========================================================
# 6.4 CREATE FULL-DATASET HOVER LOOKUP
#
# Each sampled point receives information about ALL
# movies sharing its exact runtime-rating coordinates.
# =========================================================

if (!"group_payload" %in% names(main_scatter_data)) {
  stop(
    "group_payload is missing. Run the main-scatterplot ",
    "data preparation chunk before this regression section."
  )
}

coordinate_key <- function(x, y) {

  paste0(
    sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(x)),
    "|",
    sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(y))
  )

}


payload_lookup <- main_scatter_data %>%

  distinct(
    length,
    rating,
    group_payload
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    coord_key = coordinate_key(length, rating)
  )


# Attach the full-dataset payload to the sampled rows

plot_sample <- plot_sample %>%

  select(
    -any_of("group_payload")
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    payload_lookup %>%
      select(
        length,
        rating,
        group_payload
      ),
    by = c("length", "rating")
  )


# =========================================================
# 6.5 BUILD THE REGRESSION PLOT USING GGPLOT2
#
# Important:
# Each observed genre-border colour is constructed
# as a separate ggplot2 point layer.
#
# This preserves the individual border colours without
# passing a mapped 'colour' attribute into ggplotly.
# =========================================================

linear_plot <- ggplot()


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# CREATE INDIVIDUAL POINT LAYERS FOR GENRE BORDER COLOURS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

point_border_values <- sort(
  unique(
    na.omit(plot_sample$genre_border)
  )
)


point_border_layers <- lapply(

  point_border_values,

  function(border_colour) {

    geom_point(

      data = filter(
        plot_sample,
        genre_border == border_colour
      ),

      mapping = aes(
        x = length,
        y = rating,
        fill = film_type
      ),

      inherit.aes = FALSE,

      shape = 21,

      colour = border_colour,

      size = 1.6,

      stroke = 0.6,

      alpha = 0.5,

      show.legend = TRUE

    )

  }
)


# Add every genre-border point layer to the ggplot

for (point_layer in point_border_layers) {

  linear_plot <- linear_plot + point_layer

}


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# OTHER FILMS: RED DASHED REGRESSION LINE
# ---------------------------------------------------------

linear_plot <- linear_plot +

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      line_data,
      line_group == "Other films"
    ),

    aes(
      x = length,
      y = predicted,
      linetype = "Other films"
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = "#D62728",

    linewidth = 1.2

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # SHORT FILMS: BLUE DASHED REGRESSION LINE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      line_data,
      line_group == "Short films"
    ),

    aes(
      x = length,
      y = predicted,
      linetype = "Short films"
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = "#0072B2",

    linewidth = 1.2

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # ALL FILMS: BLACK SOLID REGRESSION LINE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      line_data,
      line_group == "All films"
    ),

    aes(
      x = length,
      y = predicted,
      linetype = "All films"
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = "black",

    linewidth = 1.2

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # FILM TYPE INTERIOR COLOURS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_fill_manual(

    name = "Film classification",

    values = film_fill

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # REGRESSION LINE LEGEND
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_linetype_manual(

    name = "Regression lines",

    values = c(

      "Other films" = "dashed",

      "Short films" = "dashed",

      "All films" = "solid"

    )

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # AXES
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_continuous(

    breaks = seq(0, 300, 30)

  ) +


  coord_cartesian(

    xlim = c(0, 300),

    ylim = c(1, 10)

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LABELS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  labs(

    title = "Linear Relationship Between Duration and Rating",

    subtitle = paste(
      "Red dashed = other films;",
      "blue dashed = short films;",
      "black solid = all films."
    ),

    x = "Movie duration (minutes)",

    y = "Average IMDb rating"

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # THEME AND LEGENDS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(

    legend.position = "right",

    legend.box = "vertical",

    legend.background = element_rect(
      fill = "white",
      colour = "#BFC5CC"
    ),

    legend.title = element_text(
      face = "bold",
      size = 10
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 9
    )

  ) +

  guides(

    fill = guide_legend(
      order = 1,
      override.aes = list(
        alpha = 1,
        size = 3
      )
    ),

    linetype = guide_legend(
      order = 2
    )

  )


# =========================================================
# 6.6 CONVERT THE GGPLOT2 FIGURE INTO INTERACTIVE PLOTLY
# =========================================================

linear_plotly <- plotly::ggplotly(

  linear_plot,

  tooltip = c("x", "y")

)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# ATTACH FULL-DATASET CUSTOMDATA TO POINT TRACES
# ---------------------------------------------------------

for (i in seq_along(linear_plotly$x$data)) {

  trace <- linear_plotly$x$data[[i]]


  # Process only marker traces

  is_marker_trace <-

    !is.null(trace$mode) &&

    grepl(
      "markers",
      trace$mode,
      fixed = TRUE
    )


  if (is_marker_trace) {

    trace_x <- as.numeric(
      unlist(trace$x)
    )

    trace_y <- as.numeric(
      unlist(trace$y)
    )


    trace_keys <- coordinate_key(
      trace_x,
      trace_y
    )


    matched_rows <- match(
      trace_keys,
      payload_lookup$coord_key
    )


    # Complete group payload for every displayed point

    trace$customdata <- unname(
      as.character(
        payload_lookup$group_payload[matched_rows]
      )
    )


    # Suppress standard tooltip but retain JavaScript events

    trace$hoverinfo <- "none"


    linear_plotly$x$data[[i]] <- trace

  }


  # Disable tooltip interaction on regression lines

  is_line_trace <-

    !is.null(trace$mode) &&

    grepl(
      "lines",
      trace$mode,
      fixed = TRUE
    )


  if (is_line_trace) {

    trace$hoverinfo <- "skip"

    linear_plotly$x$data[[i]] <- trace

  }

}


# =========================================================
# 6.7 CREATE A CLEAN HORIZONTAL LEGEND
#
# Five entries:
# 1. Other films: orange point
# 2. Short films: blue point
# 3. Other films: red dashed line
# 4. Short films: blue dashed line
# 5. All films: black solid line
#
# Legend positioned below the X-axis title.
# No legend box or background.
# =========================================================


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. HIDE AUTOMATIC GGPLOTLY LEGEND ENTRIES
# ---------------------------------------------------------

for (i in seq_along(linear_plotly$x$data)) {

  trace <- linear_plotly$x$data[[i]]

  trace$showlegend <- FALSE

  linear_plotly$x$data[[i]] <- trace

}


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. ADD FIVE CUSTOM LEGEND ENTRIES
#
# Coordinates (0, 0) are outside the visible Y range
# of 1 to 10, so these traces won't appear on the graph.
# Unlike NA placeholders, these are valid observations.
# ---------------------------------------------------------

linear_plotly <- linear_plotly %>%


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # OTHER FILMS: ORANGE CIRCLE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  plotly::add_trace(

    x = c(0, 0),

    type = "scatter",

  # -------------------------------------------------------

  plotly::add_trace(

    marker = list(

    ),

    name = "Short films",

    showlegend = TRUE,

  ) %>%


  # -------------------------------------------------------

  # -------------------------------------------------------

  plotly::add_trace(

    type = "scatter",

    mode = "lines",

    line = list(
      color = "#D62728",

    ),

    name = "Other films (fit)",

    showlegend = TRUE,

  ) %>%


  # -------------------------------------------------------

  # -------------------------------------------------------

  plotly::add_trace(

    line = list(

      width = 2.5
    ),

    name = "Short films (fit)",

    showlegend = TRUE,

    hoverinfo = "skip"

  ) %>%


  # -------------------------------------------------------

  # -------------------------------------------------------

  plotly::add_trace(

  # -------------------------------------------------------

  plotly::layout(

    legend = list(

      orientation = "h",

      x = 0.5,

      y = -0.28,

      xanchor = "center",

      yanchor = "top",

      bgcolor = "rgba(255,255,255,0)",

      borderwidth = 0,

        size = 10
      ),

      traceorder = "normal"

    ),

    margin = list(

      b = 145

    )

  )

# =========================================================
# 6.8 ROTATING MOVIE SELECTOR
#
# Initial hover delay: 2 seconds
# Movie display duration: 3 seconds
# =========================================================

linear_plotly <- htmlwidgets::onRender(

  linear_plotly,

  r"(
  function(el, x) {

    const gd = el;


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // A. CREATE THE OVERLAY
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    gd.style.position = "relative";

    const overlay = document.createElement("div");

    overlay.style.cssText = `
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      width: 100%;
      height: 100%;
      z-index: 50;
      pointer-events: none;
      overflow: hidden;
    `;


    const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

    const svg = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "svg"
    );

    svg.style.cssText = `
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      width: 100%;
      height: 100%;
    `;


    const cardLayer = document.createElement("div");

    cardLayer.style.cssText = `
      position: absolute;
      inset: 0;
      width: 100%;
      height: 100%;
    `;


    overlay.appendChild(svg);

    overlay.appendChild(cardLayer);

    gd.appendChild(overlay);


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // B. ANIMATION STATE
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    let rotationTimer = null;

    let startTimer = null;

    let unhoverTimer = null;

    let activeKey = null;

    let currentIndex = 0;

    let activeMovies = [];

    let activeAnchor = null;


    function stopRotation() {

      if (rotationTimer !== null) {

        clearInterval(rotationTimer);

        rotationTimer = null;

      }

    }


    function clearDisplay() {

      stopRotation();


      if (startTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(startTimer);

        startTimer = null;

      }


      if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

        unhoverTimer = null;

      }


      svg.innerHTML = "";

      cardLayer.innerHTML = "";

      activeKey = null;

      activeMovies = [];

      activeAnchor = null;

      currentIndex = 0;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // C. HELPER FUNCTIONS
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function clamp(value, min, max) {

      return Math.min(
        Math.max(value, min),
        max
      );

    }


    function addText(parent, tag, value, css) {

      const node = document.createElement(tag);

      node.textContent =
        value === null || value === undefined
          ? "Not recorded"
          : String(value);

      if (css) {

        node.style.cssText = css;

      }

      parent.appendChild(node);

      return node;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // D. DRAW CONNECTING WIRE
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function drawWire(

      anchorX,
      anchorY,
      cardX,
      cardY,
      colour,
      cardWidth,
      cardHeight

    ) {

      const dx = cardX - anchorX;

      const dy = cardY - anchorY;

      const distance = Math.sqrt(
        dx * dx + dy * dy
      );

      if (distance < 1) return;


      const ux = dx / distance;

      const uy = dy / distance;


      const startX = anchorX + ux * 18;

      const startY = anchorY + uy * 18;


      const factor = 1 / Math.max(

        Math.abs(dx) / (cardWidth / 2),

        Math.abs(dy) / (cardHeight / 2)

      );


      const endX = cardX - dx * factor;

      const endY = cardY - dy * factor;


      const line = document.createElementNS(
        svgNS,
        "line"
      );

      line.setAttribute("x1", startX);

      line.setAttribute("y1", startY);

      line.setAttribute("x2", endX);

      line.setAttribute("y2", endY);

      line.setAttribute("stroke", colour);

      line.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2.5");

      line.setAttribute("stroke-opacity", "0.85");

      svg.appendChild(line);

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // E. DRAW CENTRAL HUB
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function drawHub(anchorX, anchorY, total) {

      const circle = document.createElementNS(
        svgNS,
        "circle"
      );

      circle.setAttribute("cx", anchorX);

      circle.setAttribute("cy", anchorY);

      circle.setAttribute("r", "18");

      circle.setAttribute("fill", "#263238");

      circle.setAttribute("stroke", "#FFFFFF");

      circle.setAttribute("stroke-width", "3");

      svg.appendChild(circle);


      const number = document.createElementNS(
        svgNS,
        "text"
      );

      number.setAttribute("x", anchorX);

      number.setAttribute("y", anchorY + 4);

      number.setAttribute("text-anchor", "middle");

      number.setAttribute("font-size", "11");

      number.setAttribute("font-weight", "bold");

      number.setAttribute("fill", "#FFFFFF");

      number.textContent = total;

      svg.appendChild(number);

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // F. CREATE INDIVIDUAL MOVIE CARD
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function createMovieCard(movie, index, total) {

      const filmColour =
        movie.film_colour || "#777777";

      const genreColour =
        movie.genre_border || "#AAAAAA";


      const serial =
        String(index + 1).padStart(2, "0");

      const totalSerial =
        String(total).padStart(2, "0");


      const card = document.createElement("div");

      card.style.cssText = `
        position: absolute;
        width: 260px;
        min-height: 160px;
        box-sizing: border-box;
        padding: 13px;
        background: rgba(255,255,255,0.98);
        border: 2px solid ${filmColour};
        border-left: 7px solid ${genreColour};
        border-radius: 12px;
        box-shadow: 0 6px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.23);
        color: #263238;
        font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
        line-height: 1.4;
        transform: translate(-50%, -50%);
        animation: movieCardAppear 0.25s ease-out;
      `;


      // Header

      const header = document.createElement("div");

      header.style.cssText = `
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: space-between;
        margin-bottom: 9px;
      `;


      // Serial number

      addText(

        header,

        "span",

        `MOVIE ${serial} / ${totalSerial}`,

        `
          font-size: 13px;
          font-weight: bold;
          color: ${filmColour};
          letter-spacing: 0.5px;
        `

      );


      // Film classification

      addText(

        header,

        "span",

        movie.film_type,

        `
          font-size: 10px;
          font-weight: bold;
          color: ${filmColour};
          border: 1px solid ${filmColour};
          border-radius: 12px;
          padding: 3px 7px;
        `

      );


      card.appendChild(header);


      // Movie title

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `${movie.title} (${movie.year})`,

        `
          font-size: 15px;
          font-weight: bold;
          color: #17202A;
          margin-bottom: 7px;
        `

      );


      // Runtime, rating and votes

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `${movie.length} min  ·  Rating ${movie.rating}  ·  Votes ${movie.votes}`,

        `
          font-size: 11px;
          margin-bottom: 6px;
        `

      );


      // Genres

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `Genres: ${movie.genre}`,

        `
          font-size: 11px;
          margin-bottom: 6px;
          color: #46545F;
        `

      );


      // Budget

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `Budget: ${movie.budget}`,

        `
          font-size: 10px;
          color: #64717B;
        `

      );


      // MPAA

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `MPAA: ${movie.mpaa}`,

        `
          font-size: 10px;
          color: #64717B;
        `

      );


      cardLayer.appendChild(card);

      return card;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // G. DISPLAY ONE MOVIE
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    function renderMovie(index) {

      if (!activeMovies.length || !activeAnchor) {

        return;

      }


      const total = activeMovies.length;

      const movie = activeMovies[index];

      const anchorX = activeAnchor.x;

      const anchorY = activeAnchor.y;

      const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


      svg.innerHTML = "";

      cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


      const cardWidth = 260;

      const cardHeight = 160;

      const radius = 185;


      // Rotate clockwise around the selected point

      const angle =
        -Math.PI / 2 +
        (2 * Math.PI * index / total);


      let cardX =
        anchorX + radius * Math.cos(angle);

      let cardY =
        anchorY + radius * Math.sin(angle);


      // Keep card within plot boundaries

      const leftBound =
        size.l + cardWidth / 2 + 5;

      const rightBound =
        size.l + size.w - cardWidth / 2 - 5;

      const topBound =
        size.t + cardHeight / 2 + 5;

      const bottomBound =
        size.t + size.h - cardHeight / 2 - 5;


      cardX = clamp(
        cardX,
        leftBound,
        rightBound
      );

      cardY = clamp(
        cardY,
        topBound,
        bottomBound
      );


      // Connecting wire

      drawWire(

        anchorX,
        anchorY,

        cardX,
        cardY,

        movie.film_colour || "#777777",

        cardWidth,
        cardHeight

      );


      // Central hub

      drawHub(
        anchorX,
        anchorY,
        total
      );


      // Movie card

      const card = createMovieCard(
        movie,
        index,
        total
      );

      card.style.left = `${cardX}px`;

      card.style.top = `${cardY}px`;

    }


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // H. HANDLE HOVER EVENTS
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    gd.on("plotly_hover", function(eventData) {

      if (
        !eventData ||
        !eventData.points ||
        eventData.points.length === 0
      ) {

        return;

      }


      // Cancel pending unhover reset

      if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

        unhoverTimer = null;

      }


      const point = eventData.points[0];

      const key = `${point.x}|${point.y}`;


      // Do not restart on repeated hover events
      // at the same coordinate.

      if (key === activeKey) {

        return;

      }


      // Cancel previous animation and delay

      stopRotation();


      if (startTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(startTimer);

        startTimer = null;

      }


      svg.innerHTML = "";

      cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


      // -------------------------------------------------
      // READ ALL MOVIES AT THIS COORDINATE
      // -------------------------------------------------

      let raw = point.customdata;


      if (
        Array.isArray(raw) &&
        raw.length === 1 &&
        typeof raw[0] === "string"
      ) {

        raw = raw[0];

      }


      // Fallback to trace customdata

      if (
        raw === undefined &&
        point.data &&
        point.data.customdata
      ) {

        raw = point.data.customdata[
          point.pointNumber
        ];

      }


      let movies;

      try {

        movies = typeof raw === "string"
          ? JSON.parse(raw)
          : raw;

      } catch (error) {

        console.error(
          "Could not read grouped movie information:",
          error
        );

        return;

      }


      if (!Array.isArray(movies)) {

        movies = [movies];

      }


      if (!movies.length) {

        return;

      }


      // Store the new selection

      activeKey = key;

      activeMovies = movies;

      currentIndex = 0;


      // Convert data coordinates to pixel coordinates

      const xAxis = point.xaxis;

      const yAxis = point.yaxis;

      const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


      const anchorX =

        (xAxis._offset || size.l) +

        xAxis.d2p(point.x);


      const anchorY =

        (yAxis._offset || size.t) +

        yAxis.d2p(point.y);


      activeAnchor = {

        x: anchorX,

        y: anchorY

      };


      // -------------------------------------------------
      // INITIAL 2-SECOND DELAY
      // -------------------------------------------------

      startTimer = setTimeout(function() {

        startTimer = null;


        if (
          activeKey !== key ||
          !activeMovies.length ||
          !activeAnchor
        ) {

          return;

        }


        // Display the first movie

        currentIndex = 0;

        renderMovie(0);


        // -------------------------------------------------
        // ROTATE EVERY 3 SECONDS
        // -------------------------------------------------

        if (activeMovies.length > 1) {

          rotationTimer = setInterval(function() {

            if (activeKey !== key) {

              stopRotation();

              return;

            }


            currentIndex =

              (currentIndex + 1) % activeMovies.length;


            renderMovie(currentIndex);

          }, 3000);

        }

      }, 2000);

    });


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // I. HANDLE UNHOVER
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    gd.on("plotly_unhover", function() {

      if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

        clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      }


      // Brief grace period for overlapping traces

      unhoverTimer = setTimeout(function() {

        clearDisplay();

      }, 80);

    });


    // Leaving the chart stops all timers

    gd.addEventListener(
      "mouseleave",
      clearDisplay
    );


    // ---------------------------------------------------
    // J. CARD APPEARANCE ANIMATION
    // ---------------------------------------------------

    const style = document.createElement("style");

    style.textContent = `

      @keyframes movieCardAppear {

        from {

          opacity: 0;

          transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scale(0.93);

        }

        to {

          opacity: 1;

          transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scale(1);

        }

      }

    `;

    document.head.appendChild(style);

  }
  )"
)


# =========================================================
# 6.9 DISPLAY FINAL INTERACTIVE REGRESSION PLOT
# =========================================================

linear_plotly

```

# 7. Genre-specific runtime and rating relationships

A movie can belong to several genres.

For example, a movie classified as both Comedy and Drama is included in both genre analyses.

```{r genre-linear-plots}
# =========================================================
# SECTION 7: GENRE-SPECIFIC DURATION AND RATING ANALYSIS
#
# Six separate interactive ggplot2-based charts:
# Action, Animation, Comedy, Documentary, Drama, Romance.
#
# Regression calculations use complete datasets.
# Displayed points are sampled.
#
# Hover carousel:
# Initial delay = 2 seconds
# Display duration = 3 seconds per movie
# =========================================================


# =========================================================
# 7.1 CONVERT GENRE INDICATORS INTO LONG FORMAT
# =========================================================

movies_genres <- movies_display %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(rating),
    !is.na(length)
  ) %>%

  pivot_longer(

    cols = all_of(genres),

    names_to = "genre",

    values_to = "in_genre"

  ) %>%

  filter(
    in_genre == 1
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    genre = factor(
      genre,
      levels = genres
    ),

    film_type = as.character(film_type),

    film_colour = unname(
      film_fill[film_type]
    ),

    # Preserve genre-border colours
    genre_border = ifelse(
      is.na(genre_border),
      "#808080",
      as.character(genre_border)
    ),

    # Budget
    budget_display = ifelse(
      is.na(budget),
      "Not recorded",
      scales::dollar(budget, accuracy = 1)
    ),

    # MPAA
    mpaa_display = ifelse(
      is.na(mpaa) |
        trimws(as.character(mpaa)) == "",
      "Not recorded",
      as.character(mpaa)
    ),

    # Votes
    votes_display = ifelse(
      is.na(votes),
      "Not recorded",
      scales::comma(votes)
    ),

    # Complete genre combination
    genre_combination = ifelse(
      is.na(genre_combination) |
        trimws(as.character(genre_combination)) == "",
      "No recorded genre",
      as.character(genre_combination)
    )

  ) %>%

  arrange(
    genre,
    length,
    rating,
    film_type,
    title,
    year
  )


# =========================================================
# 7.2 CREATE GENRE-SPECIFIC HOVER GROUPS
#
# Grouping is performed using:
# Genre + Runtime + Rating.
#
# This prevents movies from different genres from being
# combined into the same carousel.
# =========================================================

genre_hover_groups <- movies_genres %>%

  group_by(
    genre,
    length,
    rating
  ) %>%

  group_modify(~ {

    dat <- .x

    group_info <- .y

    movie_cards <- lapply(

      seq_len(nrow(dat)),

      function(i) {

        list(

          title = as.character(dat$title[i]),

          year = ifelse(
            is.na(dat$year[i]),
            "Unknown",
            as.character(dat$year[i])
          ),

          panel_genre = as.character(
            group_info$genre[[1]]
          ),

          length = group_info$length[[1]],

          rating = group_info$rating[[1]],

          votes = dat$votes_display[i],

          film_type = dat$film_type[i],

          film_colour = dat$film_colour[i],

          genre = dat$genre_combination[i],

          genre_border = dat$genre_border[i],

          budget = dat$budget_display[i],

          mpaa = dat$mpaa_display[i]

        )

      }

    )

    tibble::tibble(

      group_payload = as.character(

        jsonlite::toJSON(

          movie_cards,

          auto_unbox = TRUE,

          na = "null"

        )

      )

    )

  }) %>%

  ungroup()


# Attach the complete movie groups to each observation

movies_genres <- movies_genres %>%

  left_join(

    genre_hover_groups,

    by = c(
      "genre",
      "length",
      "rating"
    )

  )


# =========================================================
# 7.3 GENRE-SPECIFIC REGRESSION EQUATIONS
#
# All equations are calculated using the full datasets.
# =========================================================

genre_equations <- purrr::map_dfr(

  genres,

  function(g) {

    d <- filter(
      movies_genres,
      as.character(genre) == g
    )

    bind_rows(

      linear_summary(

        filter(
          d,
          film_type == "Other film"
        ),

        paste(g, "- Other films")

      ),

      linear_summary(

        filter(
          d,
          film_type == "Short film"
        ),

        paste(g, "- Short films")

      ),

      linear_summary(

        d,

        paste(g, "- All films")

      )

    )

  }

)


clean_table(

  genre_equations,

  "Genre-specific regression equations",

  digits = 5

)


# =========================================================
# 7.4 PRECOMPUTE ALL GENRE-SPECIFIC REGRESSION LINES
#
# Each line uses its complete corresponding dataset.
# =========================================================

genre_line_data <- purrr::map_dfr(

  genres,

  function(g) {

    d <- filter(
      movies_genres,
      as.character(genre) == g
    )

    bind_rows(

      make_lm_line(

        filter(
          d,
          film_type == "Other film"
        ),

        yvar = "rating",

        label = "Other films"

      ),

      make_lm_line(

        filter(
          d,
          film_type == "Short film"
        ),

        yvar = "rating",

        label = "Short films"

      ),

      make_lm_line(

        d,

        yvar = "rating",

        label = "All films"

      )

    ) %>%

      mutate(

        genre = factor(
          g,
          levels = genres
        )

      )

  }

)


# =========================================================
# 7.5 CREATE THE FIVE-ITEM HTML LEGEND
#
# No Plotly dummy observations are used.
# This guarantees that the line indicators are visible.
#
# Legend consists of:
# Orange circle = Other films
# Blue circle = Short films
# Red dashed = Other films fit
# Blue dashed = Short films fit
# Black solid = All films fit
# =========================================================

make_genre_legend <- function() {

  make_item <- function(label, mark_type, colour) {

    if (mark_type == "point") {

      mark_style <- paste0(
        "display:inline-block;",
        "width:10px;",
        "height:10px;",
        "border-radius:50%;",
        "background:", colour, ";",
        "flex-shrink:0;"
      )

    } else if (mark_type == "dashed") {

      mark_style <- paste0(
        "display:inline-block;",
        "width:27px;",
        "height:0;",
        "border-top:2.5px dashed ", colour, ";",
        "flex-shrink:0;"
      )

    } else {

      mark_style <- paste0(
        "display:inline-block;",
        "width:27px;",
        "height:0;",
        "border-top:2.5px solid ", colour, ";",
        "flex-shrink:0;"
      )

    }


    htmltools::tags$div(

      style = paste(
        "display:flex;",
        "align-items:center;",
        "gap:7px;",
        "white-space:nowrap;",
        "font-family:Arial,sans-serif;",
        "font-size:11px;",
        "color:#38434D;"
      ),

      htmltools::tags$span(
        style = mark_style
      ),

      htmltools::tags$span(label)

    )

  }


  htmltools::tags$div(

    style = paste(
      "display:flex;",
      "flex-wrap:wrap;",
      "justify-content:center;",
      "align-items:center;",
      "gap:12px 22px;",
      "padding:12px 8px 24px;",
      "width:100%;",
      "box-sizing:border-box;"
    ),

    make_item(
      "Other films",
      "point",
      film_fill[["Other film"]]
    ),

    make_item(
      "Short films",
      "point",
      film_fill[["Short film"]]
    ),

    make_item(
      "Other films (fit)",
      "dashed",
      "#D62728"
    ),

    make_item(
      "Short films (fit)",
      "dashed",
      "#0072B2"
    ),

    make_item(
      "All films (fit)",
      "solid",
      "black"
    )

  )

}


# =========================================================
# 7.6 PREPARE THE REUSABLE GENRE CAROUSEL JAVASCRIPT
#
# Initial hover delay: 2000 ms
# Display duration: 3000 ms per movie
# =========================================================

genre_carousel_js <- r"(
function(el, x) {

  const gd = el;


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // A. CREATE OVERLAY
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.style.position = "relative";

  const overlay = document.createElement("div");

  overlay.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
    z-index:50;
    pointer-events:none;
    overflow:hidden;
  `;


  const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

  const svg = document.createElementNS(
    svgNS,
    "svg"
  );

  svg.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
  `;


  const cardLayer = document.createElement("div");

  cardLayer.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
  `;


  overlay.appendChild(svg);

  overlay.appendChild(cardLayer);

  gd.appendChild(overlay);


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // B. ANIMATION STATE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  let rotationTimer = null;

  let startTimer = null;

  let unhoverTimer = null;

  let activeKey = null;

  let currentIndex = 0;

  let activeMovies = [];

  let activeAnchor = null;


  function stopRotation() {

    if (rotationTimer !== null) {

      clearInterval(rotationTimer);

      rotationTimer = null;

    }

  }


  function clearDisplay() {

    stopRotation();


    if (startTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(startTimer);

      startTimer = null;

    }


    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      unhoverTimer = null;

    }


    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";

    activeKey = null;

    activeMovies = [];

    activeAnchor = null;

    currentIndex = 0;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // C. HELPERS
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function clamp(value, min, max) {

    return Math.min(
      Math.max(value, min),
      max
    );

  }


  function addText(parent, tag, value, css) {

    const node = document.createElement(tag);

    node.textContent =
      value === null || value === undefined
        ? "Not recorded"
        : String(value);

    if (css) {

      node.style.cssText = css;

    }

    parent.appendChild(node);

    return node;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // D. CONNECTING WIRE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function drawWire(

    anchorX,
    anchorY,
    cardX,
    cardY,
    colour,
    cardWidth,
    cardHeight

  ) {

    const dx = cardX - anchorX;

    const dy = cardY - anchorY;

    const distance = Math.sqrt(
      dx * dx + dy * dy
    );

    if (distance < 1) return;


    const ux = dx / distance;

    const uy = dy / distance;


    const startX = anchorX + ux * 18;

    const startY = anchorY + uy * 18;


    const factor = 1 / Math.max(

      Math.abs(dx) / (cardWidth / 2),

      Math.abs(dy) / (cardHeight / 2)

    );


    const endX = cardX - dx * factor;

    const endY = cardY - dy * factor;


    const line = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "line"
    );

    line.setAttribute("x1", startX);

    line.setAttribute("y1", startY);

    line.setAttribute("x2", endX);

    line.setAttribute("y2", endY);

    line.setAttribute("stroke", colour);

    line.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2.5");

    line.setAttribute("stroke-opacity", "0.85");

    svg.appendChild(line);

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // E. CENTRAL HUB
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function drawHub(anchorX, anchorY, total) {

    const circle = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "circle"
    );

    circle.setAttribute("cx", anchorX);

    circle.setAttribute("cy", anchorY);

    circle.setAttribute("r", "18");

    circle.setAttribute("fill", "#263238");

    circle.setAttribute("stroke", "#FFFFFF");

    circle.setAttribute("stroke-width", "3");

    svg.appendChild(circle);


    const number = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "text"
    );

    number.setAttribute("x", anchorX);

    number.setAttribute("y", anchorY + 4);

    number.setAttribute("text-anchor", "middle");

    number.setAttribute("font-size", "11");

    number.setAttribute("font-weight", "bold");

    number.setAttribute("fill", "#FFFFFF");

    number.textContent = total;

    svg.appendChild(number);

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // F. INDIVIDUAL MOVIE CARD
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function createMovieCard(movie, index, total) {

    const filmColour =
      movie.film_colour || "#777777";

    const genreColour =
      movie.genre_border || "#AAAAAA";


    const serial =
      String(index + 1).padStart(2, "0");

    const totalSerial =
      String(total).padStart(2, "0");


    const card = document.createElement("div");

    card.style.cssText = `
      position:absolute;
      width:260px;
      min-height:160px;
      box-sizing:border-box;
      padding:13px;
      background:rgba(255,255,255,0.98);
      border:2px solid ${filmColour};
      border-left:7px solid ${genreColour};
      border-radius:12px;
      box-shadow:0 6px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.23);
      color:#263238;
      font-family:Arial,sans-serif;
      line-height:1.4;
      transform:translate(-50%,-50%);
      animation:genreMovieCardAppear 0.25s ease-out;
    `;


    // Header

    const header = document.createElement("div");

    header.style.cssText = `
      display:flex;
      align-items:center;
      justify-content:space-between;
      margin-bottom:9px;
    `;


    // Serial number

    addText(

      header,

      "span",

      `MOVIE ${serial} / ${totalSerial}`,

      `
        font-size:13px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:${filmColour};
        letter-spacing:0.5px;
      `

    );


    // Film classification

    addText(

      header,

      "span",

      movie.film_type,

      `
        font-size:10px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:${filmColour};
        border:1px solid ${filmColour};
        border-radius:12px;
        padding:3px 7px;
      `

    );


    card.appendChild(header);


    // Movie title

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `${movie.title} (${movie.year})`,

      `
        font-size:15px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:#17202A;
        margin-bottom:7px;
      `

    );


    // Genre panel

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Panel: ${movie.panel_genre}`,

      `
        font-size:11px;
        font-weight:bold;
        margin-bottom:5px;
      `

    );


    // Runtime, rating and votes

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `${movie.length} min · Rating ${movie.rating} · Votes ${movie.votes}`,

      `
        font-size:11px;
        margin-bottom:6px;
      `

    );


    // Full genre combination

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Genres: ${movie.genre}`,

      `
        font-size:11px;
        margin-bottom:6px;
        color:#46545F;
      `

    );


    // Budget

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Budget: ${movie.budget}`,

      `
        font-size:10px;
        color:#64717B;
      `

    );


    // MPAA

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `MPAA: ${movie.mpaa}`,
```
