```{r genre-linear-plots}
      `
        font-size:10px;
        color:#64717B;
      `

    );


    cardLayer.appendChild(card);

    return card;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // G. RENDER ONE MOVIE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function renderMovie(index) {

    if (!activeMovies.length || !activeAnchor) {

      return;

    }


    const total = activeMovies.length;

    const movie = activeMovies[index];

    const anchorX = activeAnchor.x;

    const anchorY = activeAnchor.y;

    const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


    const cardWidth = 260;

    const cardHeight = 160;

    const radius = 185;


    // Clockwise movement

    const angle =
      -Math.PI / 2 +
      (2 * Math.PI * index / total);


    let cardX =
      anchorX + radius * Math.cos(angle);

    let cardY =
      anchorY + radius * Math.sin(angle);


    // Keep the card inside the chart

    const leftBound =
      size.l + cardWidth / 2 + 5;

    const rightBound =
      size.l + size.w - cardWidth / 2 - 5;

    const topBound =
      size.t + cardHeight / 2 + 5;

    const bottomBound =
      size.t + size.h - cardHeight / 2 - 5;


    cardX = clamp(
      cardX,
      leftBound,
      rightBound
    );

    cardY = clamp(
      cardY,
      topBound,
      bottomBound
    );


    // Connecting wire

    drawWire(

      anchorX,
      anchorY,

      cardX,
      cardY,

      movie.film_colour || "#777777",

      cardWidth,
      cardHeight

    );


    // Central hub

    drawHub(
      anchorX,
      anchorY,
      total
    );


    // Movie card

    const card = createMovieCard(
      movie,
      index,
      total
    );

    card.style.left = `${cardX}px`;

    card.style.top = `${cardY}px`;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // H. HANDLE HOVER EVENTS
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.on("plotly_hover", function(eventData) {

    if (
      !eventData ||
      !eventData.points ||
      eventData.points.length === 0
    ) {

      return;

    }


    // Cancel pending unhover

    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      unhoverTimer = null;

    }


    const point = eventData.points[0];

    const key = `${point.x}|${point.y}`;


    // Do not restart for repeated hover events
    // at the same coordinate.

    if (key === activeKey) {

      return;

    }


    // Cancel earlier animation and delay

    stopRotation();


    if (startTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(startTimer);

      startTimer = null;

    }


    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


    // Read grouped movie information

    let raw = point.customdata;


    if (
      Array.isArray(raw) &&
      raw.length === 1 &&
      typeof raw[0] === "string"
    ) {

      raw = raw[0];

    }


    // Fallback to trace customdata

    if (
      raw === undefined &&
      point.data &&
      point.data.customdata
    ) {

      raw = point.data.customdata[
        point.pointNumber
      ];

    }


    let movies;

    try {

      movies = typeof raw === "string"
        ? JSON.parse(raw)
        : raw;

    } catch (error) {

      console.error(
        "Could not read genre movie information:",
        error
      );

      return;

    }


    if (!Array.isArray(movies)) {

      movies = [movies];

    }


    if (!movies.length) {

      return;

    }


    // Store the selected coordinate group

    activeKey = key;

    activeMovies = movies;

    currentIndex = 0;


    // Convert data coordinates into pixel coordinates

    const xAxis = point.xaxis;

    const yAxis = point.yaxis;

    const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


    const anchorX =

      (xAxis._offset || size.l) +

      xAxis.d2p(point.x);


    const anchorY =

      (yAxis._offset || size.t) +

      yAxis.d2p(point.y);


    activeAnchor = {

      x: anchorX,

      y: anchorY

    };


    // -------------------------------------------------
    // INITIAL 2-SECOND DELAY
    // -------------------------------------------------

    startTimer = setTimeout(function() {

      startTimer = null;


      if (
        activeKey !== key ||
        !activeMovies.length ||
        !activeAnchor
      ) {

        return;

      }


      // Display movie 01

      currentIndex = 0;

      renderMovie(0);


      // -------------------------------------------------
      // ROTATE EVERY 3 SECONDS
      // -------------------------------------------------

      if (activeMovies.length > 1) {

        rotationTimer = setInterval(function() {

          if (activeKey !== key) {

            stopRotation();

            return;

          }


          currentIndex =

            (currentIndex + 1) % activeMovies.length;


          renderMovie(currentIndex);

        }, 3000);

      }

    }, 2000);

  });


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // I. HANDLE UNHOVER
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.on("plotly_unhover", function() {

    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

    }


    // Small grace period when moving between point traces

    unhoverTimer = setTimeout(function() {

      clearDisplay();

    }, 80);

  });


  // Leaving the chart stops all timers

  gd.addEventListener(
    "mouseleave",
    clearDisplay
  );


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // J. CARD APPEARANCE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  const style = document.createElement("style");

  style.textContent = `

    @keyframes genreMovieCardAppear {

      from {

        opacity:0;

        transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(0.93);

      }

      to {

        opacity:1;

        transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(1);

      }

    }

  `;

  document.head.appendChild(style);

}
)"


# =========================================================
# 7.7 CREATE ONE SEPARATE INTERACTIVE GENRE PLOT
#
# This function is called once for every genre.
# =========================================================

make_genre_widget <- function(g) {


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # A. EXTRACT THE COMPLETE GENRE DATASET
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  d <- movies_genres %>%

    filter(
      as.character(genre) == g
    ) %>%

    arrange(
      length,
      rating,
      film_type,
      title,
      year
    )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # B. SAMPLE POINTS FOR DISPLAY
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  genre_sample <- sample_by_groups(

    d,

    group_vars = "film_type",

    max_n = 1000

  )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # C. CREATE A COMPLETE COORDINATE LOOKUP
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  genre_lookup <- d %>%

    distinct(
      length,
      rating,
      group_payload
    ) %>%

    mutate(

      coord_key = paste0(

        sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(length)),

        "|",

        sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(rating))

      )

    )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # D. IDENTIFY OBSERVED GENRE BORDER COLOURS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  border_values <- sort(

    unique(
      na.omit(genre_sample$genre_border)
    )

  )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # E. START THE GGPLOT2 PLOT
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  p <- ggplot()


  # Each observed genre border colour is constructed
  # as its own ggplot2 layer.
  #
  # This avoids the earlier Plotly mapped-colour issue.

  for (border_colour in border_values) {

    p <- p +

      geom_point(

        data = filter(
          genre_sample,
          genre_border == border_colour
        ),

        mapping = aes(
          x = length,
          y = rating,
          fill = film_type
        ),

        inherit.aes = FALSE,

        shape = 21,

        colour = border_colour,

        size = 1.6,

        alpha = 0.5,

        stroke = 0.6,

        show.legend = FALSE

      )

  }


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # F. OTHER FILMS: RED DASHED REGRESSION LINE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  p <- p +

    geom_line(

      data = filter(
        genre_line_data,
        as.character(genre) == g,
        line_group == "Other films"
      ),

      aes(
        x = length,
        y = predicted,
        group = 1
      ),

      inherit.aes = FALSE,

      colour = "#D62728",

      linetype = "dashed",

      linewidth = 1.1,

      show.legend = FALSE

    ) +


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # G. SHORT FILMS: BLUE DASHED REGRESSION LINE
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    geom_line(

      data = filter(
        genre_line_data,
        as.character(genre) == g,
        line_group == "Short films"
      ),

      aes(
        x = length,
        y = predicted,
        group = 1
      ),

      inherit.aes = FALSE,

      colour = "#0072B2",

      linetype = "dashed",

      linewidth = 1.1,

      show.legend = FALSE

    ) +


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # H. ALL FILMS: BLACK SOLID REGRESSION LINE
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    geom_line(

      data = filter(
        genre_line_data,
        as.character(genre) == g,
        line_group == "All films"
      ),

      aes(
        x = length,
        y = predicted,
        group = 1
      ),

      inherit.aes = FALSE,

      colour = "black",

      linetype = "solid",

      linewidth = 1.2,

      show.legend = FALSE

    )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # I. FINISH THE GGPLOT2 CHART
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  p <- p +

    scale_fill_manual(
      values = film_fill
    ) +

    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(0, 300, 30)
    ) +

    coord_cartesian(
      xlim = c(0, 300),
      ylim = c(1, 10)
    ) +

    labs(

      title = paste(
        g,
        ": Movie Duration vs Average IMDb Rating"
      ),

      subtitle = paste(
        "Red dashed = other films;",
        "blue dashed = short films;",
        "black solid = all films."
      ),

      x = "Movie duration (minutes)",

      y = "Average IMDb rating"

    ) +

    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

    theme(

      legend.position = "none",

      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 15
      ),

      plot.subtitle = element_text(
        size = 10
      ),

      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()

    )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # J. CONVERT GGPLOT2 TO PLOTLY
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  widget <- plotly::ggplotly(

    p,

    tooltip = c("x", "y")

  )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # K. ATTACH FULL-DATASET CUSTOMDATA TO POINT TRACES
  #
  # Regression lines are not modified.
  # Every visible point receives the complete movie
  # group associated with its exact coordinate.
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  for (i in seq_along(widget$x$data)) {

    trace <- widget$x$data[[i]]


    is_marker_trace <-

      !is.null(trace$mode) &&

      grepl(
        "markers",
        trace$mode,
        fixed = TRUE
      )


    if (is_marker_trace) {


      trace_x <- suppressWarnings(

        as.numeric(
          unlist(trace$x)
        )

      )


      trace_y <- suppressWarnings(

        as.numeric(
          unlist(trace$y)
        )

      )


      trace_keys <- paste0(

        sprintf("%.8f", trace_x),

        "|",

        sprintf("%.8f", trace_y)

      )


      matched_rows <- match(

        trace_keys,

        genre_lookup$coord_key

      )


      trace$customdata <- unname(

        as.character(
          genre_lookup$group_payload[matched_rows]
        )

      )


      # Keep JavaScript hover events enabled

      trace$hoverinfo <- "none"

      trace$showlegend <- FALSE


      widget$x$data[[i]] <- trace


    } else {


      # No tooltips or automatic legends for regression lines

      trace$hoverinfo <- "skip"

      trace$showlegend <- FALSE


      widget$x$data[[i]] <- trace

    }

  }


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # L. PLOTLY LAYOUT
  #
  # The legend is deliberately disabled here.
  # A separate HTML legend is placed underneath the chart.
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  widget <- widget %>%

    plotly::layout(

      hovermode = "closest",

      showlegend = FALSE,

      margin = list(
        t = 80,
        b = 60,
        l = 65,
        r = 25
      )

    ) %>%

    plotly::config(

      displaylogo = FALSE,

      responsive = TRUE

    )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # M. ATTACH THE ROTATING MOVIE SELECTOR
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  widget <- htmlwidgets::onRender(

    widget,

    genre_carousel_js

  )


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # N. RETURN THE CHART AND HTML LEGEND TOGETHER
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  htmltools::tagList(

    widget,

    make_genre_legend()

  )

}


# =========================================================
# 7.8 GENERATE THE SIX SEPARATE GENRE PLOTS
# =========================================================

set.seed(2026)

genre_plot_widgets <- purrr::map(

  genres,

  make_genre_widget

)

names(genre_plot_widgets) <- genres


# =========================================================
# 7.9 DISPLAY ALL SIX PLOTS SEPARATELY
#
# Every genre has its own full-width interactive chart.
# Every chart has its own five-item legend underneath.
# =========================================================

genre_plots_output <- htmltools::tagList(

  lapply(

    genres,

    function(g) {

      htmltools::tags$div(

        style = paste(
          "width:100%;",
          "margin-bottom:38px;"
        ),

        htmltools::tags$h3(

          g,

          style = paste(
            "font-family:Arial,sans-serif;",
            "font-size:19px;",
            "font-weight:600;",
            "margin:25px 0 8px;"
          )

        ),

        genre_plot_widgets[[g]]

      )

    }

  )

)


# Display the six separate interactive plots

genre_plots_output

```

# 8. Movie duration vs popularity

The number of votes is used as a proxy for audience engagement.

A logarithmic scale is used because vote counts are strongly skewed.

```{r popularity-analysis}
# =========================================================
# 8.1 PREPARE POPULARITY DATA
# =========================================================

popularity_data <- movies_display %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(length),
    !is.na(votes),
    votes > 0
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    # Logarithmic transformation of vote count
    log_votes = log10(votes),

    film_type = as.character(film_type),

    # Interior colour
    film_colour = unname(
      film_fill[film_type]
    ),

    # Genre border
    genre_border = ifelse(
      is.na(genre_border),
      "#808080",
      as.character(genre_border)
    ),

    # Format votes
    votes_display = scales::comma(votes),

    # Format budget
    budget_display = ifelse(
      is.na(budget),
      "Not recorded",
      scales::dollar(budget, accuracy = 1)
    ),

    # Format MPAA
    mpaa_display = ifelse(
      is.na(mpaa) |
        trimws(as.character(mpaa)) == "",
      "Not recorded",
      as.character(mpaa)
    ),

    # Preserve the full genre combination
    genre_combination = ifelse(
      is.na(genre_combination) |
        trimws(as.character(genre_combination)) == "",
      "No recorded genre",
      as.character(genre_combination)
    )

  ) %>%

  arrange(
    length,
    log_votes,
    film_type,
    title,
    year
  )


# =========================================================
# 8.2 CREATE POPULARITY HOVER GROUPS
#
# Movies sharing the same:
# 1. Runtime
# 2. log10(votes)
#
# are placed in the same carousel.
#
# Grouping is done using the full dataset, not the sample.
# =========================================================

popularity_hover_groups <- popularity_data %>%

  group_by(
    length,
    log_votes
  ) %>%

  group_modify(~ {

    dat <- .x

    group_info <- .y

    movie_cards <- lapply(

      seq_len(nrow(dat)),

      function(i) {

        list(

          title = as.character(dat$title[i]),

          year = ifelse(
            is.na(dat$year[i]),
            "Unknown",
            as.character(dat$year[i])
          ),

          length = group_info$length[[1]],

          log_votes = group_info$log_votes[[1]],

          votes = dat$votes_display[i],

          rating = ifelse(
            is.na(dat$rating[i]),
            "Not recorded",
            as.character(dat$rating[i])
          ),

          film_type = dat$film_type[i],

          film_colour = dat$film_colour[i],

          genre = dat$genre_combination[i],

          genre_border = dat$genre_border[i],

          budget = dat$budget_display[i],

          mpaa = dat$mpaa_display[i]

        )

      }

    )

    tibble::tibble(

      group_payload = as.character(

        jsonlite::toJSON(

          movie_cards,

          auto_unbox = TRUE,

          na = "null"

        )

      )

    )

  }) %>%

  ungroup()


# Attach complete movie groups

popularity_data <- popularity_data %>%

  left_join(

    popularity_hover_groups,

    by = c(
      "length",
      "log_votes"
    )

  )


# =========================================================
# 8.3 FIT THE THREE POPULARITY RELATIONSHIPS
#
# All three regression lines use the COMPLETE dataset.
# =========================================================

popularity_line_data <- bind_rows(

  make_lm_line(

    filter(
      popularity_data,
      film_type == "Other film"
    ),

    yvar = "log_votes",

    label = "Other films"

  ),

  make_lm_line(

    filter(
      popularity_data,
      film_type == "Short film"
    ),

    yvar = "log_votes",

    label = "Short films"

  ),

  make_lm_line(

    popularity_data,

    yvar = "log_votes",

    label = "All films"

  )

)


# =========================================================
# 8.4 SAMPLE POINTS FOR DISPLAY
#
# Maximum 2500 observations per film classification.
# Regression calculations still use all observations.
# =========================================================

set.seed(2026)

popularity_sample <- sample_by_groups(

  popularity_data,

  group_vars = "film_type",

  max_n = 2500

)


# =========================================================
# 8.5 CREATE THE GGPLOT2 POPULARITY PLOT
#
# Each genre-border colour is constructed separately
# to avoid the earlier ggplotly colour warnings.
#
# Interior = film classification.
# Border = genre combination.
# =========================================================

popularity_border_values <- sort(

  unique(
    na.omit(popularity_sample$genre_border)
  )

)


# Start with an empty ggplot2 object

popularity_plot <- ggplot()


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# INDIVIDUAL MOVIE POINT LAYERS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

popularity_point_layers <- lapply(

  popularity_border_values,

  function(border_colour) {

    geom_point(

      data = filter(
        popularity_sample,
        genre_border == border_colour
      ),

      mapping = aes(

        x = length,

        y = log_votes,

        fill = film_type

      ),

      inherit.aes = FALSE,

      shape = 21,

      colour = border_colour,

      size = 1.4,

      alpha = 0.4,

      stroke = 0.5,

      show.legend = FALSE

    )

  }

)


# Add all point layers

for (point_layer in popularity_point_layers) {

  popularity_plot <- popularity_plot + point_layer

}


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# OTHER FILMS: RED DASHED REGRESSION LINE
# ---------------------------------------------------------

popularity_plot <- popularity_plot +

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      popularity_line_data,
      line_group == "Other films"
    ),

    aes(
      x = length,
      y = predicted,
      group = 1
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = "#D62728",

    linetype = "dashed",

    linewidth = 1

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # SHORT FILMS: BLUE DASHED REGRESSION LINE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      popularity_line_data,
      line_group == "Short films"
    ),

    aes(
      x = length,
      y = predicted,
      group = 1
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = "#0072B2",

    linetype = "dashed",

    linewidth = 1

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # ALL FILMS: BLACK SOLID REGRESSION LINE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      popularity_line_data,
      line_group == "All films"
    ),

    aes(
      x = length,
      y = predicted,
      group = 1
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = "black",

    linetype = "solid",

    linewidth = 1

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # FILM-TYPE FILL COLOURS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_fill_manual(

    values = film_fill

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LOGARITHMIC AXIS LABELS
  #
  # 0 = 1 vote
  # 1 = 10 votes
  # 2 = 100 votes
  # 3 = 1,000 votes
  # 4 = 10,000 votes
  # 5 = 100,000 votes
  # 6 = 1,000,000 votes
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(

    breaks = 0:6,

    labels = function(x) {

      scales::comma(10^x)

    }

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # X-AXIS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_continuous(

    breaks = seq(0, 300, 30)

  ) +


  coord_cartesian(

    xlim = c(0, 300)

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # TITLES AND LABELS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  labs(

    title = "Movie Duration vs Number of Votes",

    subtitle = paste(

      "Logarithmic Y-axis;",
      "red dashed = other films;",
      "blue dashed = short films;",
      "black solid = all films."

    ),

    x = "Movie duration (minutes)",

    y = "Number of IMDb votes"

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # THEME
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(

    legend.position = "none",

    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()

  )


# =========================================================
# 8.6 CONVERT GGPLOT2 INTO INTERACTIVE PLOTLY
# =========================================================

popularity_plotly <- plotly::ggplotly(

  popularity_plot,

  tooltip = c("x", "y")

)


# =========================================================
# 8.7 ATTACH FULL-DATASET HOVER INFORMATION
#
# Each sampled point receives the complete movie group
# sharing its runtime and logarithmic vote coordinate.
# =========================================================

popularity_lookup <- popularity_data %>%

  distinct(

    length,

    log_votes,

    group_payload

  ) %>%

  mutate(

    coord_key = paste0(

      sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(length)),

      "|",

      sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(log_votes))

    )

  )


popularity_coord_key <- function(x, y) {

  paste0(

    sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(x)),

    "|",

    sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(y))

  )

}


for (i in seq_along(popularity_plotly$x$data)) {

  trace <- popularity_plotly$x$data[[i]]


  # Identify point traces

  is_marker_trace <-

    !is.null(trace$mode) &&

    grepl(
      "markers",
      trace$mode,
      fixed = TRUE
    )


  if (is_marker_trace) {

    trace_x <- suppressWarnings(

      as.numeric(
        unlist(trace$x)
      )

    )

    trace_y <- suppressWarnings(

      as.numeric(
        unlist(trace$y)
      )

    )


    trace_keys <- popularity_coord_key(

      trace_x,

      trace_y

    )


    matched_rows <- match(

      trace_keys,

      popularity_lookup$coord_key

    )


    # Attach the complete movie list

    trace$customdata <- unname(

      as.character(
        popularity_lookup$group_payload[matched_rows]
      )

    )


    # Suppress standard tooltip but retain JS hover events

    trace$hoverinfo <- "none"

    trace$showlegend <- FALSE


    popularity_plotly$x$data[[i]] <- trace

  } else {

    # Regression lines do not need hover tooltips

    trace$hoverinfo <- "skip"

    trace$showlegend <- FALSE


    popularity_plotly$x$data[[i]] <- trace

  }

}


# =========================================================
# 8.8 CREATE THE FIVE-ITEM HTML LEGEND
#
# No Plotly dummy traces.
# No automatic legend entries.
# No enclosing legend box.
# =========================================================

make_popularity_legend <- function() {


  make_item <- function(label, mark_type, colour) {


    if (mark_type == "point") {

      mark_style <- paste0(

        "display:inline-block;",

        "width:10px;",

        "height:10px;",

        "border-radius:50%;",

        "background:", colour, ";",

        "flex-shrink:0;"

      )

    } else if (mark_type == "dashed") {

      mark_style <- paste0(

        "display:inline-block;",

        "width:27px;",

        "height:0;",

        "border-top:2.5px dashed ", colour, ";",

        "flex-shrink:0;"

      )

    } else {

      mark_style <- paste0(

        "display:inline-block;",

        "width:27px;",

        "height:0;",

        "border-top:2.5px solid ", colour, ";",

        "flex-shrink:0;"

      )

    }


    htmltools::tags$div(

      style = paste(

        "display:flex;",

        "align-items:center;",

        "gap:7px;",

        "white-space:nowrap;",

        "font-family:Arial,sans-serif;",

        "font-size:11px;",

        "color:#38434D;"

      ),

      htmltools::tags$span(
        style = mark_style
      ),

      htmltools::tags$span(label)

    )

  }


  htmltools::tags$div(

    style = paste(

      "display:flex;",

      "flex-wrap:wrap;",

      "justify-content:center;",

      "align-items:center;",

      "gap:12px 22px;",

      "padding:12px 8px 24px;",

      "width:100%;",

      "box-sizing:border-box;"

    ),


    make_item(
      "Other films",
      "point",
      film_fill[["Other film"]]
    ),


    make_item(
      "Short films",
      "point",
      film_fill[["Short film"]]
    ),


    make_item(
      "Other films (fit)",
      "dashed",
      "#D62728"
    ),


    make_item(
      "Short films (fit)",
      "dashed",
      "#0072B2"
    ),


    make_item(
      "All films (fit)",
      "solid",
      "black"
    )

  )

}


# =========================================================
# 8.9 FINAL PLOTLY LAYOUT
# =========================================================

popularity_plotly <- popularity_plotly %>%

  plotly::layout(

    title = list(

      text = "Movie Duration vs Number of Votes",

      x = 0.02

    ),

    xaxis = list(

      title = "Movie duration (minutes)",

      range = c(0, 300),

      dtick = 30,

      gridcolor = "#E5E5E5"

    ),

    yaxis = list(

      title = "Number of IMDb votes",

      type = "linear",

      tickmode = "array",

      tickvals = 0:6,

      ticktext = scales::comma(10^(0:6)),

      gridcolor = "#E5E5E5"

    ),

    hovermode = "closest",

    showlegend = FALSE,

    margin = list(

      t = 80,

      b = 55,

      l = 80,

      r = 25

    )

  ) %>%

  plotly::config(

    displaylogo = FALSE,

    responsive = TRUE

  )


# =========================================================
# 8.10 ROTATING POPULARITY MOVIE SELECTOR
#
# Initial hover delay = 2 seconds
# Movie display duration = 3 seconds
# One movie = static card after delay
# Multiple movies = clockwise carousel
# =========================================================

popularity_carousel_js <- r"(
function(el, x) {

  const gd = el;


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // A. CREATE OVERLAY
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.style.position = "relative";

  const overlay = document.createElement("div");

  overlay.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
    z-index:50;
    pointer-events:none;
    overflow:hidden;
  `;


  const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

  const svg = document.createElementNS(
    svgNS,
    "svg"
  );

  svg.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
  `;


  const cardLayer = document.createElement("div");

  cardLayer.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
  `;


  overlay.appendChild(svg);

  overlay.appendChild(cardLayer);

  gd.appendChild(overlay);


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // B. ANIMATION STATE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  let rotationTimer = null;

  let startTimer = null;

  let unhoverTimer = null;

  let activeKey = null;

  let currentIndex = 0;

  let activeMovies = [];

  let activeAnchor = null;


  function stopRotation() {

    if (rotationTimer !== null) {

      clearInterval(rotationTimer);

      rotationTimer = null;

    }

  }


  function clearDisplay() {

    stopRotation();


    if (startTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(startTimer);

      startTimer = null;

    }


    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      unhoverTimer = null;

    }


    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";

    activeKey = null;

    activeMovies = [];

    activeAnchor = null;

    currentIndex = 0;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // C. HELPERS
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function clamp(value, min, max) {

    return Math.min(
      Math.max(value, min),
      max
    );

  }


  function addText(parent, tag, value, css) {

    const node = document.createElement(tag);

    node.textContent =
      value === null || value === undefined
        ? "Not recorded"
        : String(value);

    if (css) {

      node.style.cssText = css;

    }

    parent.appendChild(node);

    return node;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // D. CONNECTING WIRE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function drawWire(

    anchorX,
    anchorY,
    cardX,
    cardY,
    colour,
    cardWidth,
    cardHeight

  ) {

    const dx = cardX - anchorX;

    const dy = cardY - anchorY;

    const distance = Math.sqrt(
      dx * dx + dy * dy
    );

    if (distance < 1) return;


    const ux = dx / distance;

    const uy = dy / distance;


    const startX = anchorX + ux * 18;

    const startY = anchorY + uy * 18;


    const factor = 1 / Math.max(

      Math.abs(dx) / (cardWidth / 2),

      Math.abs(dy) / (cardHeight / 2)

    );


    const endX = cardX - dx * factor;

    const endY = cardY - dy * factor;


    const line = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "line"
    );

    line.setAttribute("x1", startX);

    line.setAttribute("y1", startY);

    line.setAttribute("x2", endX);

    line.setAttribute("y2", endY);

    line.setAttribute("stroke", colour);

    line.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2.5");

    line.setAttribute("stroke-opacity", "0.85");

    svg.appendChild(line);

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // E. CENTRAL HUB
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function drawHub(anchorX, anchorY, total) {

    const circle = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "circle"
    );

    circle.setAttribute("cx", anchorX);

    circle.setAttribute("cy", anchorY);

    circle.setAttribute("r", "18");

    circle.setAttribute("fill", "#263238");

    circle.setAttribute("stroke", "#FFFFFF");

    circle.setAttribute("stroke-width", "3");

    svg.appendChild(circle);


    const number = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "text"
    );

    number.setAttribute("x", anchorX);

    number.setAttribute("y", anchorY + 4);

    number.setAttribute("text-anchor", "middle");

    number.setAttribute("font-size", "11");

    number.setAttribute("font-weight", "bold");

    number.setAttribute("fill", "#FFFFFF");

    number.textContent = total;

    svg.appendChild(number);

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // F. CREATE MOVIE CARD
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function createMovieCard(movie, index, total) {

    const filmColour =
      movie.film_colour || "#777777";

    const genreColour =
      movie.genre_border || "#AAAAAA";


    const serial =
      String(index + 1).padStart(2, "0");

    const totalSerial =
      String(total).padStart(2, "0");


    const card = document.createElement("div");

    card.style.cssText = `
      position:absolute;
      width:270px;
      min-height:175px;
      box-sizing:border-box;
      padding:13px;
      background:rgba(255,255,255,0.98);
      border:2px solid ${filmColour};
      border-left:7px solid ${genreColour};
      border-radius:12px;
      box-shadow:0 6px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.23);
      color:#263238;
      font-family:Arial,sans-serif;
      line-height:1.4;
      transform:translate(-50%,-50%);
      animation:popularityMovieCardAppear 0.25s ease-out;
    `;


    // Header

    const header = document.createElement("div");

    header.style.cssText = `
      display:flex;
      align-items:center;
      justify-content:space-between;
      margin-bottom:9px;
    `;


    // Serial number

    addText(

      header,

      "span",

      `MOVIE ${serial} / ${totalSerial}`,

      `
        font-size:13px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:${filmColour};
        letter-spacing:0.5px;
      `

    );


    // Film classification

    addText(

      header,

      "span",

      movie.film_type,

      `
        font-size:10px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:${filmColour};
        border:1px solid ${filmColour};
        border-radius:12px;
        padding:3px 7px;
      `

    );


    card.appendChild(header);


    // Movie title

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `${movie.title} (${movie.year})`,

      `
        font-size:15px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:#17202A;
        margin-bottom:7px;
      `

    );


    // Runtime and rating

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `${movie.length} min · Rating ${movie.rating}`,

      `
        font-size:11px;
        margin-bottom:5px;
      `

    );


    // Votes

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `IMDb votes: ${movie.votes}`,

      `
        font-size:12px;
        font-weight:bold;
        margin-bottom:4px;
      `

    );


    // Log-transformed votes

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `log10(votes): ${Number(movie.log_votes).toFixed(3)}`,

      `
        font-size:11px;
        margin-bottom:6px;
        color:#46545F;
      `

    );


    // Genre combination

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Genres: ${movie.genre}`,

      `
        font-size:11px;
        margin-bottom:6px;
        color:#46545F;
      `

    );


    // Budget

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Budget: ${movie.budget}`,

      `
        font-size:10px;
        color:#64717B;
      `

    );


    // MPAA

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `MPAA: ${movie.mpaa}`,

      `
        font-size:10px;
        color:#64717B;
      `

    );


    cardLayer.appendChild(card);

    return card;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // G. DISPLAY ONE MOVIE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function renderMovie(index) {

    if (!activeMovies.length || !activeAnchor) {

      return;

    }


    const total = activeMovies.length;

    const movie = activeMovies[index];

    const anchorX = activeAnchor.x;

    const anchorY = activeAnchor.y;

    const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


    const cardWidth = 270;

    const cardHeight = 175;

    const radius = 185;


    // Clockwise rotation

    const angle =
      -Math.PI / 2 +
      (2 * Math.PI * index / total);


    let cardX =
      anchorX + radius * Math.cos(angle);

    let cardY =
      anchorY + radius * Math.sin(angle);


    // Keep the card inside the plotting area

    const leftBound =
      size.l + cardWidth / 2 + 5;

    const rightBound =
      size.l + size.w - cardWidth / 2 - 5;

    const topBound =
      size.t + cardHeight / 2 + 5;

    const bottomBound =
      size.t + size.h - cardHeight / 2 - 5;


    cardX = clamp(
      cardX,
      leftBound,
      rightBound
    );

    cardY = clamp(
      cardY,
      topBound,
      bottomBound
    );


    // Connecting wire

    drawWire(

      anchorX,
      anchorY,

      cardX,
      cardY,

      movie.film_colour || "#777777",

      cardWidth,
      cardHeight

    );


    // Central hub

    drawHub(
      anchorX,
      anchorY,
      total
    );


    // Movie card

    const card = createMovieCard(
      movie,
      index,
      total
    );

    card.style.left = `${cardX}px`;

    card.style.top = `${cardY}px`;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // H. HANDLE HOVER EVENTS
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.on("plotly_hover", function(eventData) {

    if (
      !eventData ||
      !eventData.points ||
      eventData.points.length === 0
    ) {

      return;

    }


    // Cancel pending unhover reset

    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      unhoverTimer = null;

    }


    const point = eventData.points[0];

    const key = `${point.x}|${point.y}`;


    // Prevent repeated events from restarting the
    // same carousel at the same coordinate.

    if (key === activeKey) {

      return;

    }


    // Stop any previous animation

    stopRotation();


    if (startTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(startTimer);

      startTimer = null;

    }


    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


    // -------------------------------------------------
    // READ GROUPED MOVIE DATA
    // -------------------------------------------------

    let raw = point.customdata;


    if (
      Array.isArray(raw) &&
      raw.length === 1 &&
      typeof raw[0] === "string"
    ) {

      raw = raw[0];

    }


    // Fallback to trace customdata

    if (
      raw === undefined &&
      point.data &&
      point.data.customdata
    ) {

      raw = point.data.customdata[
        point.pointNumber
      ];

    }


    let movies;

    try {

      movies = typeof raw === "string"
        ? JSON.parse(raw)
        : raw;

    } catch (error) {

      console.error(
        "Could not read popularity movie information:",
        error
      );

      return;

    }


    if (!Array.isArray(movies)) {

      movies = [movies];

    }


    if (!movies.length) {

      return;

    }


    // Store the current group

    activeKey = key;

    activeMovies = movies;

    currentIndex = 0;


    // Convert chart coordinates to pixels

    const xAxis = point.xaxis;

    const yAxis = point.yaxis;

    const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


    const anchorX =

      (xAxis._offset || size.l) +

      xAxis.d2p(point.x);


    const anchorY =

      (yAxis._offset || size.t) +

      yAxis.d2p(point.y);


    activeAnchor = {

      x: anchorX,

      y: anchorY

    };


    // -------------------------------------------------
    // INITIAL 2-SECOND DELAY
    // -------------------------------------------------

    startTimer = setTimeout(function() {

      startTimer = null;


      if (
        activeKey !== key ||
        !activeMovies.length ||
        !activeAnchor
      ) {

        return;

      }


      // Display the first movie

      currentIndex = 0;

      renderMovie(0);


      // -------------------------------------------------
      // ROTATE EVERY 3 SECONDS
      // -------------------------------------------------

      if (activeMovies.length > 1) {

        rotationTimer = setInterval(function() {

          if (activeKey !== key) {

            stopRotation();

            return;

          }


          currentIndex =

            (currentIndex + 1) % activeMovies.length;


          renderMovie(currentIndex);

        }, 3000);

      }

    }, 2000);

  });


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // I. HANDLE UNHOVER
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.on("plotly_unhover", function() {

    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

    }


    // Brief grace period for transitions between traces

    unhoverTimer = setTimeout(function() {

      clearDisplay();

    }, 80);

  });


  // Leaving the chart stops all timers

  gd.addEventListener(
    "mouseleave",
    clearDisplay
  );


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // J. CARD APPEARANCE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  const style = document.createElement("style");

  style.textContent = `

    @keyframes popularityMovieCardAppear {

      from {

        opacity:0;

        transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(0.93);

      }

      to {

        opacity:1;

        transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(1);

      }

    }

  `;

  document.head.appendChild(style);

}
)"


# =========================================================
# 8.11 ATTACH THE ANIMATED SELECTOR
# =========================================================

popularity_plotly <- htmlwidgets::onRender(

  popularity_plotly,

  popularity_carousel_js

)


# =========================================================
# 8.12 DISPLAY THE FINAL POPULARITY GRAPH AND LEGEND
# =========================================================

popularity_output <- htmltools::tagList(

  popularity_plotly,

  make_popularity_legend()

)


popularity_output

```

# 9. Historical development of movie duration

## 9.1 Annual median runtime

The median runtime is calculated separately for each film classification and release year.

The shaded region represents the interquartile range.

```{r annual-runtime}

annual_runtime <- movies_analysis %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(length),
    length >= 0,
    !is.na(film_type)
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    film_type = as.character(film_type)
  ) %>%

  group_by(
    year,
    film_type
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n = n(),

    median_length = median(length),

    q25 = quantile(length, 0.25),

    q75 = quantile(length, 0.75),

    .groups = "drop"

  ) %>%

  filter(
    n >= 10
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    film_colour = unname(
      film_fill[film_type]
    ),

    # Complete annual summary information for hovering
    hover_payload = purrr::pmap_chr(

      list(
        year = year,
        film_type = film_type,
        n = n,
        median_length = median_length,
        q25 = q25,
        q75 = q75,
        film_colour = film_colour
      ),

      function(
        year,
        film_type,
        n,
        median_length,
        q25,
        q75,
        film_colour
      ) {

        as.character(

          jsonlite::toJSON(

            list(

              kind = "runtime",

              title = "Annual runtime summary",

              year = year,

              film_type = film_type,

              n = n,

              median_length = median_length,

              q25 = q25,

              q75 = q75,

              film_colour = film_colour

            ),

            auto_unbox = TRUE,

            na = "null"

          )

        )

      }

    )

  ) %>%

  arrange(
    year,
    film_type
  )
```

## 9.2 Create reusable hover and legend functions

This helper code is shared by both annual charts.

```{r annual-hover-helpers}

# =========================================================
# 9.2.1 ATTACH HOVER INFORMATION TO GGPLOTLY POINTS
#
# The charts contain two separately constructed point layers:
# 1. Other films
# 2. Short films
#
# Their order is preserved during ggplotly conversion.
# =========================================================

attach_annual_payload <- function(
    widget,
    lookup,
    y_column
) {

  film_order <- c(
    "Other film",
    "Short film"
  )

  marker_index <- 0L


  make_key <- function(x, y) {

    paste0(
      sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(x)),
      "|",
      sprintf("%.8f", as.numeric(y))
    )

  }


  for (i in seq_along(widget$x$data)) {

    trace <- widget$x$data[[i]]


    is_marker_trace <-

      !is.null(trace$mode) &&

      grepl(
        "markers",
        trace$mode,
        fixed = TRUE
      )


    if (is_marker_trace) {

      marker_index <- marker_index + 1L


      if (marker_index > length(film_order)) {

        stop(
          "Unexpected number of point traces in annual chart."
        )

      }


      current_film <- film_order[marker_index]


      # Look up only the corresponding film classification

      group_lookup <- lookup %>%

        filter(
          as.character(film_type) == current_film
        )


      trace_x <- suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(unlist(trace$x))
      )

      trace_y <- suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(unlist(trace$y))
      )


      trace_keys <- make_key(
        trace_x,
        trace_y
      )


      lookup_keys <- make_key(
        group_lookup$year,
        group_lookup[[y_column]]
      )


      matched_rows <- match(
        trace_keys,
        lookup_keys
      )


      # Attach the full annual summary as customdata

      trace$customdata <- unname(

        as.character(
          group_lookup$hover_payload[matched_rows]
        )

      )


      # JavaScript handles the custom hover card

      trace$hoverinfo <- "none"

      trace$showlegend <- FALSE


      widget$x$data[[i]] <- trace

    } else {

      # No automatic tooltips or legends for ribbons/lines

      trace$hoverinfo <- "skip"

      trace$showlegend <- FALSE

      widget$x$data[[i]] <- trace

    }

  }


  if (marker_index != 2L) {

    warning(
      "Expected exactly two annual point traces; found ",
      marker_index,
      ". Check the order of the ggplot2 point layers."
    )

  }


  widget

}


# =========================================================
# 9.2.2 CREATE A CLEAN HTML LEGEND
#
# No Plotly dummy traces.
# No surrounding legend box.
# =========================================================

make_annual_legend <- function(include_iqr = FALSE) {


  make_item <- function(label, colour, show_band = FALSE) {


    mark <- htmltools::tags$span(

      style = paste(
        "position:relative;",
        "display:inline-block;",
        "width:30px;",
        "height:12px;",
        "flex-shrink:0;"
      ),


      # IQR ribbon indicator, when applicable

      if (show_band) {

        htmltools::tags$span(

          style = paste0(
            "position:absolute;",
            "left:0;",
            "top:1px;",
            "width:30px;",
            "height:10px;",
            "background:", colour, ";",
            "opacity:0.18;"
          )

        )

      },


      # Median/count line

      htmltools::tags$span(

        style = paste0(
          "position:absolute;",
          "left:0;",
          "top:5px;",
          "width:30px;",
          "border-top:2px solid ", colour, ";"
        )

      ),


      # Point marker

      htmltools::tags$span(

        style = paste0(
          "position:absolute;",
          "left:11px;",
          "top:2px;",
          "width:7px;",
          "height:7px;",
          "border-radius:50%;",
          "background:", colour, ";",
          "border:1px solid white;"
        )

      )

    )


    htmltools::tags$div(

      style = paste(
        "display:flex;",
        "align-items:center;",
        "gap:7px;",
        "white-space:nowrap;",
        "font-family:Arial,sans-serif;",
        "font-size:11px;",
        "color:#38434D;"
      ),

      mark,

      htmltools::tags$span(label)

    )

  }


  htmltools::tags$div(

    style = paste(
      "display:flex;",
      "flex-wrap:wrap;",
      "justify-content:center;",
      "align-items:center;",
      "gap:12px 28px;",
      "padding:12px 8px 24px;",
      "width:100%;",
      "box-sizing:border-box;"
    ),


    make_item(

      if (include_iqr) {
        "Other films (median; shaded = IQR)"
      } else {
        "Other films"
      },

      film_fill[["Other film"]],

      show_band = include_iqr

    ),


    make_item(

      if (include_iqr) {
        "Short films (median; shaded = IQR)"
      } else {
        "Short films"
      },

      film_fill[["Short film"]],

      show_band = include_iqr

    )

  )

}


# =========================================================
# 9.2.3 REUSABLE ANNUAL SUMMARY HOVER CARD
#
# One static card per annual datapoint.
# Initial hover delay = 2 seconds.
# No carousel, because each point is an annual aggregate.
# =========================================================

annual_summary_hover_js <- r"(
function(el, x) {

  const gd = el;


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // A. OVERLAY
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.style.position = "relative";

  const overlay = document.createElement("div");

  overlay.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
    z-index:50;
    pointer-events:none;
    overflow:hidden;
  `;


  const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";

  const svg = document.createElementNS(
    svgNS,
    "svg"
  );

  svg.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
  `;


  const cardLayer = document.createElement("div");

  cardLayer.style.cssText = `
    position:absolute;
    inset:0;
    width:100%;
    height:100%;
  `;


  overlay.appendChild(svg);

  overlay.appendChild(cardLayer);

  gd.appendChild(overlay);


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // B. STATE AND TIMERS
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  let startTimer = null;

  let unhoverTimer = null;

  let activeKey = null;


  function clearDisplay() {

    if (startTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(startTimer);

      startTimer = null;

    }

    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      unhoverTimer = null;

    }

    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";

    activeKey = null;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // C. HELPERS
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function clamp(value, min, max) {

    return Math.min(
      Math.max(value, min),
      max
    );

  }


  function addText(parent, tag, value, css) {

    const node = document.createElement(tag);

    node.textContent =
      value === null || value === undefined
        ? "Not recorded"
        : String(value);

    if (css) {

      node.style.cssText = css;

    }

    parent.appendChild(node);

    return node;

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // D. CONNECTING WIRE
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function drawWire(
    anchorX,
    anchorY,
    cardX,
    cardY,
    colour,
    cardWidth,
    cardHeight
  ) {

    const dx = cardX - anchorX;

    const dy = cardY - anchorY;

    const distance = Math.sqrt(
      dx * dx + dy * dy
    );

    if (distance < 1) return;


    const ux = dx / distance;

    const uy = dy / distance;


    const startX = anchorX + ux * 14;

    const startY = anchorY + uy * 14;


    const factor = 1 / Math.max(

      Math.abs(dx) / (cardWidth / 2),

      Math.abs(dy) / (cardHeight / 2)

    );


    const endX = cardX - dx * factor;

    const endY = cardY - dy * factor;


    const line = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "line"
    );

    line.setAttribute("x1", startX);

    line.setAttribute("y1", startY);

    line.setAttribute("x2", endX);

    line.setAttribute("y2", endY);

    line.setAttribute("stroke", colour);

    line.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2");

    line.setAttribute("stroke-opacity", "0.8");

    svg.appendChild(line);


    const hub = document.createElementNS(
      svgNS,
      "circle"
    );

    hub.setAttribute("cx", anchorX);

    hub.setAttribute("cy", anchorY);

    hub.setAttribute("r", "6");

    hub.setAttribute("fill", colour);

    hub.setAttribute("stroke", "#FFFFFF");

    hub.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2");

    svg.appendChild(hub);

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // E. CREATE ANNUAL SUMMARY CARD
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  function renderSummary(payload, anchorX, anchorY) {

    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


    const colour =
      payload.film_colour || "#777777";


    const cardWidth = 275;

    const cardHeight = 155;


    const size = gd._fullLayout._size;

    const radius = 150;


    // Position the card to the right of the point,
    // or move it to the left near the chart boundary.

    let cardX = anchorX + radius;

    if (
      cardX + cardWidth / 2 >
      size.l + size.w
    ) {

      cardX = anchorX - radius;

    }


    let cardY = anchorY - 45;


    const leftBound =
      size.l + cardWidth / 2 + 5;

    const rightBound =
      size.l + size.w - cardWidth / 2 - 5;

    const topBound =
      size.t + cardHeight / 2 + 5;

    const bottomBound =
      size.t + size.h - cardHeight / 2 - 5;


    cardX = clamp(
      cardX,
      leftBound,
      rightBound
    );

    cardY = clamp(
      cardY,
      topBound,
      bottomBound
    );


    // Draw wire

    drawWire(

      anchorX,
      anchorY,

      cardX,
      cardY,

      colour,

      cardWidth,
      cardHeight

    );


    // Card

    const card = document.createElement("div");

    card.style.cssText = `
      position:absolute;
      width:${cardWidth}px;
      min-height:${cardHeight}px;
      box-sizing:border-box;
      padding:13px;
      background:rgba(255,255,255,0.98);
      border:2px solid ${colour};
      border-left:7px solid ${colour};
      border-radius:11px;
      box-shadow:0 6px 22px rgba(0,0,0,0.20);
      color:#263238;
      font-family:Arial,sans-serif;
      line-height:1.45;
      transform:translate(-50%,-50%);
      animation:annualSummaryAppear 0.25s ease-out;
    `;


    card.style.left = `${cardX}px`;

    card.style.top = `${cardY}px`;


    // Header

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      payload.title || "Annual summary",

      `
        font-size:14px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:#17202A;
        margin-bottom:8px;
      `

    );


    // Year

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Year: ${payload.year}`,

      `
        font-size:12px;
        margin-bottom:5px;
      `

    );


    // Film classification

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Film type: ${payload.film_type}`,

      `
        font-size:12px;
        font-weight:bold;
        color:${colour};
        margin-bottom:5px;
      `

    );


    // Movie count

    addText(

      card,

      "div",

      `Number of movies: ${Number(payload.n).toLocaleString()}`,

      `
        font-size:12px;
        margin-bottom:5px;
      `

    );


    // Runtime-specific summary

    if (payload.kind === "runtime") {

      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `Median duration: ${Number(payload.median_length).toFixed(1)} minutes`,

        `
          font-size:12px;
          margin-bottom:5px;
        `

      );


      addText(

        card,

        "div",

        `Q1: ${Number(payload.q25).toFixed(1)} min  ·  Q3: ${Number(payload.q75).toFixed(1)} min`,

        `
          font-size:11px;
          color:#53616D;
        `

      );

    }


    cardLayer.appendChild(card);

  }


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // F. HOVER EVENT
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.on("plotly_hover", function(eventData) {

    if (
      !eventData ||
      !eventData.points ||
      eventData.points.length === 0
    ) {

      return;

    }


    // Cancel pending unhover

    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

      unhoverTimer = null;

    }


    const point = eventData.points[0];


    // Read custom summary data

    let raw = point.customdata;


    if (
      Array.isArray(raw) &&
      raw.length === 1
    ) {

      raw = raw[0];

    }


    if (
      raw === undefined &&
      point.data &&
      point.data.customdata
    ) {

      raw = point.data.customdata[
        point.pointNumber
      ];

    }


    let payload;

    try {

      payload = typeof raw === "string"
        ? JSON.parse(raw)
        : raw;

    } catch (error) {

      console.error(
        "Could not read annual summary information:",
        error
      );

      return;

    }


    if (!payload) return;


    // Unique key includes year, value and film type

    const key = [
      payload.year,
      point.y,
      payload.film_type
    ].join("|");


    if (key === activeKey) {

      return;

    }


    if (startTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(startTimer);

      startTimer = null;

    }


    svg.innerHTML = "";

    cardLayer.innerHTML = "";


    activeKey = key;


    // Convert point coordinates into pixels

    const xAxis = point.xaxis;

    const yAxis = point.yaxis;

    const size = gd._fullLayout._size;


    const anchorX =

      (xAxis._offset || size.l) +

      xAxis.d2p(point.x);


    const anchorY =

      (yAxis._offset || size.t) +

      yAxis.d2p(point.y);


    // -------------------------------------------------
    // INITIAL 2-SECOND DELAY
    // -------------------------------------------------

    startTimer = setTimeout(function() {

      startTimer = null;


      if (activeKey !== key) {

        return;

      }


      renderSummary(
        payload,
        anchorX,
        anchorY
      );

    }, 2000);

  });


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // G. UNHOVER
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  gd.on("plotly_unhover", function() {

    if (unhoverTimer !== null) {

      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

    }


    unhoverTimer = setTimeout(function() {

      clearDisplay();

    }, 80);

  });


  gd.addEventListener(
    "mouseleave",
    clearDisplay
  );


  // -----------------------------------------------------
  // H. CARD ANIMATION
  // -----------------------------------------------------

  const style = document.createElement("style");

  style.textContent = `

    @keyframes annualSummaryAppear {

      from {

        opacity:0;

        transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(0.94);

      }

      to {

        opacity:1;

        transform:translate(-50%,-50%) scale(1);

      }

    }

  `;

  document.head.appendChild(style);

}
)"
```

## 9.3 Interactive historical runtime plot

The IQR ribbon and median lines are separate ggplot2 layers. The individual points carry the annual hover information.

```{r annual-runtime-plot}

# =========================================================
# BUILD THE HISTORICAL RUNTIME PLOT USING GGPLOT2
# =========================================================

historical_plot <- ggplot()


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# OTHER FILMS: IQR RIBBON
# ---------------------------------------------------------

historical_plot <- historical_plot +

  geom_ribbon(

    data = filter(
      annual_runtime,
      film_type == "Other film"
    ),

    aes(
      x = year,
      ymin = q25,
      ymax = q75
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    fill = film_fill[["Other film"]],

    alpha = 0.16,

    colour = NA

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # SHORT FILMS: IQR RIBBON
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(

    data = filter(
      annual_runtime,
      film_type == "Short film"
    ),

    aes(
      x = year,
      ymin = q25,
      ymax = q75
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    fill = film_fill[["Short film"]],

    alpha = 0.16,

    colour = NA

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # OTHER FILMS: ANNUAL MEDIAN LINE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      annual_runtime,
      film_type == "Other film"
    ),

    aes(
      x = year,
      y = median_length,
      group = 1
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = film_fill[["Other film"]],

    linewidth = 1

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # SHORT FILMS: ANNUAL MEDIAN LINE
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(

    data = filter(
      annual_runtime,
      film_type == "Short film"
    ),

    aes(
      x = year,
      y = median_length,
      group = 1
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    colour = film_fill[["Short film"]],

    linewidth = 1

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # OTHER FILMS: POINTS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(

    data = filter(
      annual_runtime,
      film_type == "Other film"
    ),

    aes(
      x = year,
      y = median_length
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    shape = 21,

    fill = film_fill[["Other film"]],

    colour = film_fill[["Other film"]],

    size = 2,

    stroke = 0.7

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # SHORT FILMS: POINTS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(

    data = filter(
      annual_runtime,
      film_type == "Short film"
    ),

    aes(
      x = year,
      y = median_length
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    shape = 21,

    fill = film_fill[["Short film"]],

    colour = film_fill[["Short film"]],

    size = 2,

    stroke = 0.7

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # X-AXIS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_continuous(

    breaks = seq(1890, 2005, 10)

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Y-AXIS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(

    breaks = seq(0, 180, 15)

  ) +


  coord_cartesian(

    xlim = c(1890, 2005),

    ylim = c(0, 180)

  ) +


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LABELS
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  labs(

    title = "Historical Changes in Movie Duration",

    subtitle = paste(
      "Annual median and interquartile range;",
      "only year/type groups with at least 10 movies."
    ),

    x = "Release year",

    y = "Median movie duration (minutes)"

  ) +


  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +

  theme(

    legend.position = "none",

    plot.title = element_text(
      face = "bold"
    ),

    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 8
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()

  )


# =========================================================
# CONVERT GGPLOT2 TO PLOTLY
# =========================================================

historical_plotly <- plotly::ggplotly(

  historical_plot,

  tooltip = c("x", "y")

)


# =========================================================
# ATTACH ANNUAL SUMMARY INFORMATION
# =========================================================

historical_plotly <- attach_annual_payload(

  historical_plotly,

  annual_runtime,

  y_column = "median_length"

)


# =========================================================
# FINAL PLOT LAYOUT
# =========================================================

historical_plotly <- historical_plotly %>%

  plotly::layout(

    hovermode = "closest",

    showlegend = FALSE,

    xaxis = list(
      title = "Release year",
      range = c(1890, 2005),
      dtick = 10,
      gridcolor = "#E5E5E5"
    ),

    yaxis = list(
      title = "Median movie duration (minutes)",
      range = c(0, 180),
      dtick = 15,
      gridcolor = "#E5E5E5"
    ),

    margin = list(
      t = 80,
      b = 55,
      l = 70,
      r = 25
    )

  ) %>%

  plotly::config(

    displaylogo = FALSE,

    responsive = TRUE

  )


# =========================================================
# ATTACH THE STATIC ANNUAL SUMMARY HOVER CARD
# =========================================================

historical_plotly <- htmlwidgets::onRender(

  historical_plotly,

  annual_summary_hover_js

)


# =========================================================
# DISPLAY GRAPH + HTML LEGEND
# =========================================================

historical_runtime_output <- htmltools::tagList(

  historical_plotly,

  make_annual_legend(
    include_iqr = TRUE
  )

)


historical_runtime_output
```

## 9.4 Number of movies released per year

```{r annual-counts}

# =========================================================
# PREPARE ANNUAL RELEASE COUNTS
# =========================================================

annual_counts <- movies_analysis %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(film_type)
  ) %>%

  mutate(
    film_type = as.character(film_type)
  ) %>%

  count(

    year,

    film_type,

    name = "n"

  ) %>%

  mutate(

    film_colour = unname(
      film_fill[film_type]
    ),

    # Complete hover information

    hover_payload = purrr::pmap_chr(

      list(
        year = year,
        film_type = film_type,
        n = n,
        film_colour = film_colour
      ),

      function(
        year,
        film_type,
        n,
        film_colour
```

# 10. Reconstructing audience ratings from r1–r10

## 10.1 Mathematical basis

The dataset contains the reported overall rating in `rating` and the approximate percentage distribution of individual ratings in `r1` through `r10`.

We can use this distribution to reconstruct an approximate weighted mean:

\[
\boxed{
\widehat R =
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{10} i r_i}
{\sum_{i=1}^{10}r_i}
}
\]

Here:

- \(i\) represents an individual rating score from 1 to 10.
- \(r_i\) represents the approximate vote-share value associated with rating \(i\).

The distribution values are rounded and midpoint-coded, so they should be treated as approximate weights rather than exact vote counts. The denominator normalises these weights, accounting for the fact that their sum may not be exactly 100.

The reconstructed average can therefore be compared with the reported rating, but exact equality is not expected.

We also calculate an approximate weighted standard deviation:

\[
\widehat{\sigma} =
\sqrt{
\frac{
\sum_{i=1}^{10}r_i(i-\widehat R)^2
}{
\sum_{i=1}^{10}r_i
}
}
\]

This describes the dispersion of individual audience ratings. A higher value indicates greater disagreement among voters, while a lower value indicates that votes are more concentrated around the average.

## 10.2 Calculate the reconstructed average and standard deviation

```{r rating-reconstruction}

# Identify the ten rating-distribution columns

rating_columns <- paste0("r", 1:10)

# Check that all required columns are present

missing_rating_columns <- setdiff(
  rating_columns,
  names(movies_analysis)
)

if (length(missing_rating_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing rating-distribution columns: ",
    paste(missing_rating_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Convert the distribution columns into a numeric matrix

rating_matrix <- vapply(
  movies_analysis[rating_columns],
  function(x) {
    suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(x)))
  },
  numeric(nrow(movies_analysis))
)

rating_matrix <- as.matrix(rating_matrix)

colnames(rating_matrix) <- rating_columns

# Rating scores corresponding to r1 through r10

rating_scores <- 1:10

# Sum of the approximate distribution weights

rating_total <- rowSums(
  rating_matrix,
  na.rm = FALSE
)

# Identify valid distributions:
# - all ten values must be present
# - all values must be finite
# - no value can be negative
# - total distribution weight must be positive

valid_distribution <- (
  complete.cases(rating_matrix) &
    rowSums(is.finite(rating_matrix)) == 10 &
    rowSums(rating_matrix < 0, na.rm = TRUE) == 0 &
    is.finite(rating_total) &
    rating_total > 0
)

# Calculate the weighted sum

weighted_total <- as.numeric(
  rating_matrix %*% rating_scores
)

# Initialise reconstructed average

rating_estimated <- rep(
  NA_real_,
  nrow(movies_analysis)
)

# Calculate the approximate weighted average

rating_estimated[valid_distribution] <-
  weighted_total[valid_distribution] /
  rating_total[valid_distribution]

# Initialise approximate standard deviation

rating_sd_estimated <- rep(
  NA_real_,
  nrow(movies_analysis)
)

# Calculate deviations from the reconstructed mean

centered_ratings <- sweep(
  rating_matrix[valid_distribution, , drop = FALSE],
  1,
  rating_estimated[valid_distribution],
  FUN = "-"
)

# Calculate weighted population variance

weighted_variance <- rowSums(
  rating_matrix[valid_distribution, , drop = FALSE] *
    centered_ratings^2
) / rating_total[valid_distribution]

# Calculate approximate weighted standard deviation

rating_sd_estimated[valid_distribution] <- sqrt(
  pmax(weighted_variance, 0)
)

# Add reconstructed values to the analytical dataset

movies_analysis$rating_estimated <- rating_estimated

movies_analysis$rating_sd_estimated <- rating_sd_estimated

# Recreate the runtime display dataset after adding new variables

movies_display <- movies_analysis %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(length),
    length >= 0,
    length <= 300
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    genre_border = if_else(
      is.na(as.character(genre_border)) |
        as.character(genre_border) == "",
      "#808080",
      as.character(genre_border)
    )
  )

```

The standard deviation is calculated as a weighted population standard deviation, treating the approximate rating distribution as the full distribution of audience votes. It is not the standard error of the mean.

## 10.3 Actual vs reconstructed rating

We compare the reconstructed ratings against the reported IMDb ratings. The agreement metrics below are calculated using every movie with both values available.

```{r rating-comparison-data}
# Keep movies with both reported and reconstructed ratings
rating_comparison <- movies_analysis %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(rating),
    is.finite(rating_estimated)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rating_discrepancy = rating - rating_estimated
  )

# Fit the relationship using the full comparison dataset
agreement_model <- lm(
  rating ~ rating_estimated,
  data = rating_comparison
)

# Calculate correlation safely
rating_correlation <- if (
  nrow(rating_comparison) >= 2 &&
    sd(rating_comparison$rating) > 0 &&
    sd(rating_comparison$rating_estimated) > 0
) {
  cor(
    rating_comparison$rating,
    rating_comparison$rating_estimated,
    method = "pearson"
  )
} else {
  NA_real_
}

# Agreement metrics using all eligible movies
rating_metrics <- tibble(
  Number_of_movies = nrow(rating_comparison),
  Pearson_correlation = rating_correlation,
  Mean_absolute_error = mean(
    abs(rating_comparison$rating_discrepancy)
  ),
  Root_mean_squared_error = sqrt(
    mean(rating_comparison$rating_discrepancy^2)
  ),
  Mean_discrepancy = mean(
    rating_comparison$rating_discrepancy
  ),
  Median_absolute_error = median(
    abs(rating_comparison$rating_discrepancy)
  ),
  Calibration_intercept = unname(coef(agreement_model)[1]),
  Calibration_slope = unname(coef(agreement_model)[2]),
  Calibration_R_squared = summary(agreement_model)$r.squared
)

clean_table(
  rating_metrics,
  "Agreement between actual and reconstructed ratings",
  digits = 4
)
```

A positive mean discrepancy means that the reported ratings are, on average, higher than the reconstructed values. A negative value means that the reconstructed values are higher. Correlation alone does not establish agreement, so the error and calibration metrics provide additional information.

## 10.4 Actual vs reconstructed rating

All eligible movies are displayed. The empirical regression line is fitted using the full dataset. The red dashed line represents perfect agreement; the black solid line represents the empirical linear relationship.

```{r actual-vs-reconstructed}
# Use every eligible observation; no visualisation sampling
rating_comparison_sample <- rating_comparison

# Fit the empirical relationship using all observations
rating_agreement_fit <- lm(
  rating ~ rating_estimated,
  data = rating_comparison
)

# Generate values for the empirical regression line
agreement_x <- seq(
  min(rating_comparison$rating_estimated, na.rm = TRUE),
  max(rating_comparison$rating_estimated, na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 200
)

agreement_line <- tibble(
  rating_estimated = agreement_x,
  predicted = predict(
    rating_agreement_fit,
    newdata = tibble(rating_estimated = agreement_x)
  )
)

# IMPORTANT: points are added first; reference/regression lines are added
# afterwards so the lines remain visible above the points.
rating_comparison_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = rating_comparison_sample,
    aes(
      x = rating_estimated,
      y = rating,
      fill = film_type
    ),
    shape = 21,
    colour = "grey25",
    size = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.45,
    stroke = 0.45,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    colour = "#D62728",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = agreement_line,
    aes(
      x = rating_estimated,
      y = predicted
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "black",
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = film_fill,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  coord_equal(
    xlim = c(1, 10),
    ylim = c(1, 10),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Actual vs Reconstructed IMDb Ratings",
    subtitle = "Red dashed = perfect agreement; black solid = empirical linear relationship.",
    x = "Reconstructed average rating",
    y = "Actual IMDb rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

rating_comparison_plot
```

## 10.5 Rating discrepancy vs movie duration

A positive discrepancy means the actual rating exceeds the reconstructed estimate. A negative discrepancy means the reconstructed estimate exceeds the actual rating. The red dashed horizontal line indicates zero discrepancy. The orange, blue and black solid lines represent other films, short films and all films, respectively.

```{r discrepancy-plot}
# Prepare the full discrepancy dataset
# All eligible observations are displayed; no sampling is performed.
discrepancy_data <- rating_comparison %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(length),

    length <= 300,
    is.finite(rating_discrepancy)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    genre_border = if_else(
      is.na(as.character(genre_border)) |
        as.character(genre_border) == "",
      "#808080",
      as.character(genre_border)
    )
  )

discrepancy_sample <- discrepancy_data

# Fit all three trends using the full discrepancy dataset
discrepancy_lines <- bind_rows(
  make_lm_line(
    filter(discrepancy_data, film_type == "Other film"),

# Add one point layer per genre-border colour. This preserves the original
# genre outline colours without mapping colour to a variable in ggplotly.
add_section10_border_points <- function(
    plot,
    data,
    xvar,
    yvar,
    point_size = 1.3,
    point_alpha = 0.35,
    point_stroke = 0.45
) {
  border_values <- sort(unique(as.character(data$genre_border)))
  border_values <- border_values[
    !is.na(border_values) & nzchar(border_values)
  ]

  if (length(border_values) == 0) {
    border_values <- "#808080"
  }

  for (border_colour in border_values) {
    border_data <- data %>%
      filter(as.character(genre_border) == border_colour)

    plot <- plot +
      geom_point(
        data = border_data,
        mapping = aes(
          x = .data[[xvar]],
          y = .data[[yvar]],
          fill = film_type
        ),
        inherit.aes = FALSE,
        shape = 21,
        colour = border_colour,
        size = point_size,
        alpha = point_alpha,
        stroke = point_stroke,
        show.legend = FALSE
      )
  }

  plot
}

# Points are deliberately added first. All lines are drawn afterwards,
# ensuring the regression/reference lines are visible above the points.
discrepancy_plot <- add_section10_border_points(
  plot = ggplot(),
  data = discrepancy_sample,
  xvar = "length",

) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    colour = "#D62728",

    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(discrepancy_lines, line_group == "Short films"),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "#0072B2",
    linewidth = 1.2

  geom_line(
    data = filter(discrepancy_lines, line_group == "All films"),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    colour = "black",
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = film_fill, drop = FALSE) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 300)) +
  labs(

    subtitle = "Red dashed = zero discrepancy; the legend identifies the point groups and three fitted trends.",
    x = "Movie duration (minutes)",
    y = "Actual rating - reconstructed rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
```
