## 10.7 Interactive hover support and movie carousel

The interactive versions retain all eligible movies. When several movies share the same plotted coordinates, hovering over that point waits two seconds and then cycles through the movies every three seconds. Leaving the point clears the card; hovering again starts at Movie 01. The carousel shows one movie at a time, with film-type colour and a genre-coloured accent.

```{r section10-interactive-helpers}
# Create a consistent key for matching plotted coordinates
section10_coord_key <- function(x, y) {
  paste(
    sprintf("%.10f", as.numeric(x)),
    sprintf("%.10f", as.numeric(y)),
    sep = "|"
  )
}

# Format individual movie fields without adding thousands separators to years
section10_card_value <- function(data, column, i) {
  if (!column %in% names(data)) {
    return("")
  }

  value <- data[[column]][i]

  if (length(value) == 0 || is.na(value)) {
    return("")
  }

  if (column == "year") {
    return(as.character(as.integer(as.numeric(value))))
  }

  if (column == "votes" && is.numeric(value)) {
    return(format(
      round(value),
      big.mark = ",",
      scientific = FALSE,
      trim = TRUE
    ))
  }

  if (is.numeric(value)) {
    return(format(
      round(value, 3),
      scientific = FALSE,
      trim = TRUE,
      nsmall = 0
    ))
  }

  as.character(value)
}

# Build a compact information record for one movie
section10_make_movie_card <- function(data, i) {
  film_type_value <- section10_card_value(data, "film_type", i)
  film_colour_value <- unname(film_fill[film_type_value])

  if (length(film_colour_value) == 0 || is.na(film_colour_value)) {
    film_colour_value <- "#808080"
  }

  genre_border_value <- section10_card_value(data, "genre_border", i)

  if (genre_border_value == "") {
    genre_border_value <- "#808080"
  }

  list(
    title = section10_card_value(data, "title", i),
    year = section10_card_value(data, "year", i),
    duration = section10_card_value(data, "length", i),
    actual_rating = section10_card_value(data, "rating", i),
    reconstructed_rating = section10_card_value(data, "rating_estimated", i),
    discrepancy = section10_card_value(data, "rating_discrepancy", i),
    variability = section10_card_value(data, "rating_sd_estimated", i),
    votes = section10_card_value(data, "votes", i),
    film_type = film_type_value,
    genres = section10_card_value(data, "genre_combination", i),
    film_colour = film_colour_value,
    genre_border = genre_border_value
  )
}

# Build one payload for each unique pair of plotted coordinates
make_section10_hover_lookup <- function(data, xvar, yvar, chart_label) {
  hover_lookup <- data %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(xvar, yvar)))) %>%
    group_modify(function(.x, .y) {
      # group_modify() removes grouping columns from .x; restore them
      movie_data <- .x
      movie_data[[xvar]] <- rep(.y[[xvar]][1], nrow(movie_data))
      movie_data[[yvar]] <- rep(.y[[yvar]][1], nrow(movie_data))

      movie_cards <- lapply(
        seq_len(nrow(movie_data)),
        function(i) section10_make_movie_card(movie_data, i)
      )

      payload <- jsonlite::toJSON(
        list(
          chart = chart_label,
          movies = movie_cards
        ),
        auto_unbox = TRUE,
        na = "null"
      )

      tibble(group_payload = as.character(payload))
    }) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      coord_key = section10_coord_key(
        .data[[xvar]],
        .data[[yvar]]
      )
    )

  hover_lookup
}

# JavaScript carousel: 2-second initial delay and 3-second rotation
section10_carousel_js <- r"---(
function(el, x, data) {
  const gd = el;
  if (!gd || !gd.on) return;

  let startTimer = null;
  let rotationTimer = null;
  let unhoverTimer = null;
  let activeKey = null;
  let activePayload = null;
  let activePoint = null;
  let currentIndex = 0;
  let movieCards = [];

  gd.style.position = "relative";

  const overlay = document.createElement("div");
  overlay.style.position = "absolute";
  overlay.style.inset = "0";
  overlay.style.zIndex = "1000";
  overlay.style.pointerEvents = "none";
  overlay.style.overflow = "hidden";
  gd.appendChild(overlay);

  const svgNS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
  const svg = document.createElementNS(svgNS, "svg");
  svg.style.position = "absolute";
  svg.style.inset = "0";
  svg.style.width = "100%";
  svg.style.height = "100%";
  svg.style.overflow = "visible";
  overlay.appendChild(svg);

  const connector = document.createElementNS(svgNS, "line");
  connector.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2");
  connector.setAttribute("opacity", "0");
  svg.appendChild(connector);

  const hub = document.createElementNS(svgNS, "circle");
  hub.setAttribute("r", "6");
  hub.setAttribute("stroke", "white");
  hub.setAttribute("stroke-width", "2");
  hub.setAttribute("opacity", "0");
  svg.appendChild(hub);

  const card = document.createElement("div");
  card.style.position = "absolute";
  card.style.top = "16px";
  card.style.right = "16px";
  card.style.width = "300px";
  card.style.maxWidth = "calc(100% - 32px)";
  card.style.boxSizing = "border-box";
  card.style.borderRadius = "12px";
  card.style.padding = "13px 15px";
  card.style.boxShadow = "0 5px 20px rgba(0,0,0,0.22)";
  card.style.borderLeft = "5px solid #808080";
  card.style.fontFamily = "Arial, sans-serif";
  card.style.fontSize = "13px";
  card.style.lineHeight = "1.45";
  card.style.color = "#202020";
  card.style.opacity = "0";
  card.style.transform = "translateY(-5px)";
  card.style.transition = "opacity 0.2s ease, transform 0.2s ease";
  card.style.display = "none";
  card.style.pointerEvents = "none";
  overlay.appendChild(card);

  function esc(value) {
    return String(value == null ? "" : value)
      .replace(/&/g, "&amp;")
      .replace(/</g, "&lt;")
      .replace(/>/g, "&gt;")
      .replace(/\"/g, "&quot;")
      .replace(/'/g, "&#039;");
  }

  function detailRow(label, value) {
    if (value === null || value === undefined || String(value).trim() === "") {
      return "";
    }
    return '<div style="margin-top:3px;"><b>' + esc(label) + ':</b> ' + esc(value) + '</div>';
  }

  function drawConnector(point, movie) {
    if (!gd._fullLayout || !point) return;

    const xa = gd._fullLayout.xaxis;
    const ya = gd._fullLayout.yaxis;
    if (!xa || !ya || !xa.d2p || !ya.d2p) return;

    const px = xa._offset + xa.d2p(Number(point.x));
    const py = ya._offset + ya.d2p(Number(point.y));
    const rootRect = gd.getBoundingClientRect();
    const cardRect = card.getBoundingClientRect();
    const ex = cardRect.left - rootRect.left;
    const ey = cardRect.top - rootRect.top + cardRect.height / 2;

    connector.setAttribute("x1", px);
    connector.setAttribute("y1", py);
    connector.setAttribute("x2", ex);
    connector.setAttribute("y2", ey);
    connector.setAttribute("stroke", movie.genre_border || "#808080");
    connector.setAttribute("opacity", "0.8");

    hub.setAttribute("cx", px);
    hub.setAttribute("cy", py);
    hub.setAttribute("fill", movie.film_colour || "#808080");
    hub.setAttribute("opacity", "1");
  }

  function renderMovie(index) {
    if (!movieCards.length || !activePayload) return;

    currentIndex = index % movieCards.length;
    const movie = movieCards[currentIndex];
    const filmType = movie.film_type || "Film";
    const background = filmType === "Short film" ? "#EAF4FC" : "#FFF5E4";
    const countLabel = "Movie " + String(currentIndex + 1).padStart(2, "0") + " / " + movieCards.length;
    const title = esc(movie.title || "Untitled movie");
    const year = movie.year ? " (" + esc(movie.year) + ")" : "";

    const chartName = String(activePayload.chart || "").toLowerCase();
    let detailRows;

    if (chartName.indexOf("variability") !== -1) {
      detailRows = [
        detailRow("Duration", movie.duration ? movie.duration + " minutes" : ""),
        detailRow("Rating variability (SD)", movie.variability),
        detailRow("Actual rating", movie.actual_rating),
        detailRow("Votes", movie.votes),
        detailRow("Genres", movie.genres)
      ];
    } else if (chartName.indexOf("discrepancy") !== -1) {
      detailRows = [
        detailRow("Duration", movie.duration ? movie.duration + " minutes" : ""),
        detailRow("Actual rating", movie.actual_rating),
        detailRow("Reconstructed rating", movie.reconstructed_rating),
        detailRow("Discrepancy", movie.discrepancy),
        detailRow("Votes", movie.votes),
        detailRow("Genres", movie.genres)
      ];
    } else {
      detailRows = [
        detailRow("Actual rating", movie.actual_rating),
        detailRow("Reconstructed rating", movie.reconstructed_rating),
        detailRow("Discrepancy", movie.discrepancy),
        detailRow("Votes", movie.votes),
        detailRow("Genres", movie.genres)
      ];
    }

    const rows = detailRows.join("");

    card.style.background = background;
    card.style.borderLeftColor = movie.genre_border || "#808080";

    card.innerHTML =
      '<div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;gap:8px;margin-bottom:7px;">' +
        '<span style="font-size:11px;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:0.6px;color:#555;">' + countLabel + '</span>' +
        '<span style="background:' + esc(movie.film_colour || "#808080") + ';color:white;padding:3px 8px;border-radius:5px;font-size:10px;font-weight:700;">' + esc(filmType) + '</span>' +
      '</div>' +
      '<div style="font-size:15px;font-weight:700;margin-bottom:7px;">' + title + year + '</div>' +
      '<div>' + rows + '</div>';

    card.style.display = "block";
    requestAnimationFrame(function() {
      card.style.opacity = "1";
      card.style.transform = "translateY(0)";
      drawConnector(activePoint, movie);
    });
  }

  function clearDisplay() {
    if (startTimer) clearTimeout(startTimer);
    if (rotationTimer) clearInterval(rotationTimer);
    if (unhoverTimer) clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);

    startTimer = null;
    rotationTimer = null;
    unhoverTimer = null;
    activeKey = null;
    activePayload = null;
    activePoint = null;
    movieCards = [];
    currentIndex = 0;

    card.style.opacity = "0";
    card.style.transform = "translateY(-5px)";

    setTimeout(function() {
      if (!activePayload) {
        card.style.display = "none";
        connector.setAttribute("opacity", "0");
        hub.setAttribute("opacity", "0");
      }
    }, 220);
  }

  function scheduleClear() {
    if (unhoverTimer) clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);
    unhoverTimer = setTimeout(clearDisplay, 140);
  }

  function getPointKey(point) {
    let raw = point.customdata;

    if ((raw === undefined || raw === null) && point.data && point.pointNumber !== undefined) {
      const cd = point.data.customdata;
      if (cd && cd[point.pointNumber] !== undefined) raw = cd[point.pointNumber];
    }

    while (Array.isArray(raw) && raw.length === 1) raw = raw[0];
    return raw === undefined || raw === null ? null : String(raw);
  }

  function readPayload(point) {
    const key = getPointKey(point);
    if (!key || !data || data[key] === undefined) return null;

    try {
      return typeof data[key] === "string" ? JSON.parse(data[key]) : data[key];
    } catch (error) {
      return null;
    }
  }

  gd.on("plotly_hover", function(eventData) {
    if (unhoverTimer) {
      clearTimeout(unhoverTimer);
      unhoverTimer = null;
    }

    if (!eventData || !eventData.points || !eventData.points.length) return;

    const point = eventData.points[0];
    const key = getPointKey(point);
    const payload = readPayload(point);

    if (!key || !payload || !payload.movies || !payload.movies.length) return;

    // Repeated hover events on the same coordinate do not restart the carousel.
    if (key === activeKey) {
      activePoint = point;
      return;
    }

    clearDisplay();
    activeKey = key;
    activePayload = payload;
    activePoint = point;
    movieCards = payload.movies;
    currentIndex = 0;

    // Wait two seconds before showing Movie 01.
    startTimer = setTimeout(function() {
      if (!activePayload) return;
      renderMovie(0);

      // A single movie remains static; overlapping movies rotate every 3 seconds.
      if (movieCards.length > 1) {
        rotationTimer = setInterval(function() {
          if (!activePayload) return;
          renderMovie((currentIndex + 1) % movieCards.length);
        }, 3000);
      }
    }, 2000);
  });

  gd.on("plotly_unhover", scheduleClear);
  gd.addEventListener("mouseleave", scheduleClear);
}
)---"

# Convert a ggplot2 plot to Plotly, attach compact coordinate keys, and
# pass the coordinate-to-movie payload map once to the carousel.
make_section10_plotly <- function(plot, hover_data, xvar, yvar, chart_label) {
  hover_lookup <- make_section10_hover_lookup(
    data = hover_data,
    xvar = xvar,
    yvar = yvar,
    chart_label = chart_label
  )

  # Named list becomes a JavaScript object: coordinate key -> movie payload.
  payload_map <- stats::setNames(
    as.list(hover_lookup$group_payload),
    hover_lookup$coord_key
  )

  widget <- plotly::ggplotly(
    plot,
    tooltip = c("x", "y")
  )

  for (i in seq_along(widget$x$data)) {
    trace <- widget$x$data[[i]]
    trace_mode <- trace$mode

    is_marker_trace <- (
      !is.null(trace_mode) &&
        grepl("markers", trace_mode, fixed = TRUE)
    )

    if (
      is_marker_trace &&
        !is.null(trace$x) &&
        !is.null(trace$y)
    ) {
      trace_keys <- section10_coord_key(
        unlist(trace$x),
        unlist(trace$y)
      )

      trace$customdata <- as.character(trace_keys)
      trace$hoverinfo <- "none"
      trace$hovertemplate <- NULL
      trace$showlegend <- FALSE
    } else {
      trace$hoverinfo <- "skip"
      trace$showlegend <- FALSE
    }

    widget$x$data[[i]] <- trace
  }

  widget <- plotly::layout(
    widget,
    hovermode = "closest",
    showlegend = FALSE
  )

  htmlwidgets::onRender(
    widget,
    section10_carousel_js,
    data = payload_map
  )
}

# Custom bottom legend. Point symbols identify film classification;
# line symbols identify reference/regression lines.

make_section10_legend <- function(items) {

  legend_items <- lapply(items, function(item) {

    if (identical(item$type, "point")) {

      symbol <- htmltools::tags$span(
        style = paste0(
          "display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;",
          "border-radius:50%;",
          "background:", item$colour, ";",
          "border:1px solid #444;flex:0 0 auto;"
        )
      )

    } else {

      line_style <- if (
        identical(item$linetype, "dashed")
      ) "dashed" else "solid"

      symbol <- htmltools::tags$span(
        style = paste0(
          "display:inline-block;width:34px;",
          "border-top:3px ",
          line_style, " ", item$colour, ";",
          "flex:0 0 auto;"
        )
      )
    }

    htmltools::tags$div(

      style = paste(
        "display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;",
        "white-space:nowrap;margin:3px 12px;"
      ),

      symbol,

      htmltools::tags$span(
        style = "color:#000000 !important; font-weight:500;",
        item$label
      )
    )
  })

  htmltools::tags$div(

    style = paste(
      "display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;justify-content:center;",
      "align-items:center;gap:5px 8px;width:100%;",
      "margin:10px 0 24px 0;font-size:13px;",
      "color:#000000 !important;"
    ),

    htmltools::tagList(legend_items)
  )
}
```

## 10.9 Methodological considerations and limitations

The mathematical reconstruction of IMDb ratings provides an approximate way to examine the relationship between the distribution of individual audience votes and the reported overall rating. However, several methodological considerations must be acknowledged:

1. Approximation of the reconstructed mean: The reconstructed average is an approximation because the r1–r10 distribution values are rounded and midpoint-coded. Normalising the weights accounts for differences in their total, but the original, exact average cannot be recovered from these binned values.

2. Dependence on the original voting data: The reported rating and the r1–r10 distributions originate from the same underlying audience-voting data. Consequently, this analysis should be interpreted as a mathematical reconstruction and consistency check rather than an independent validation of IMDb ratings.

3. Interpretation of rating variability: The reconstructed standard deviation provides an approximate measure of disagreement among audience ratings. It describes the dispersion of individual votes and should not be interpreted as the standard error or uncertainty of the reported average rating.

4. Full-data analysis and interactive visualisation: All regression models, agreement statistics, and fitted trends are calculated using the complete eligible datasets. The non-interactive visualisations display all eligible observations, whereas the interactive plots display a maximum of 2,500 randomly sampled movies per film classification to improve rendering performance. The interactive carousel uses the full underlying dataset to retrieve movies sharing the coordinates of a displayed point.

These limitations should be considered when interpreting the results, particularly when comparing reconstructed ratings across films or investigating relationships between movie duration and audience-rating variability.

# 11. Budget and MPAA metadata analysis

Each movie belongs to exactly one of four metadata categories:

1. Neither budget nor MPAA recorded.
2. Budget recorded, MPAA missing.
3. MPAA recorded, budget missing.
4. Both budget and MPAA recorded.

## 11.1 Metadata summary

```{r metadata-summary}

metadata_palette <- c(
  "Neither recorded" = "#999999",
  "Budget only" = "#E69F00",
  "MPAA only" = "#56B4E9",
  "Both recorded" = "#009E73"
)

metadata_summary <- movies_analysis %>%
  filter(!is.na(metadata_group)) %>%
  group_by(metadata_group) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),

    Percentage = 100 * n() / nrow(movies_analysis),

    Median_year = median(year, na.rm = TRUE),

    Mean_runtime = mean(length, na.rm = TRUE),

    Median_runtime = median(length, na.rm = TRUE),

    Mean_rating = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE),

    Median_rating = median(rating, na.rm = TRUE),

    Median_budget = median(budget, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

clean_table(
  metadata_summary,
  "Movie characteristics by budget and MPAA availability"
)

```

## 11.2 Stacked counts by release decade

Every stack represents the total number of movies released during a particular decade, divided into the four metadata categories.

Labels are displayed only when a segment is sufficiently large relative to the overall chart height. This prevents text from spilling into neighbouring segments.

All segment counts remain available through hover, including segments without internal labels.

```{r metadata-decade}

metadata_decade <- movies_analysis %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(metadata_group)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    decade = floor(year / 10) * 10,
    metadata_group = factor(
      metadata_group,
      levels = names(metadata_palette)
    )
  ) %>%
  count(
    decade,
    metadata_group,
    .drop = TRUE
  ) %>%
  group_by(decade) %>%
  mutate(
    decade_total = sum(n),

    proportion = n / decade_total,

    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", decade, "s</b>",
      "<br>Metadata category: ", metadata_group,
      "<br>Movies: ", scales::comma(n),
      "<br>Share of decade: ",
      scales::percent(proportion, accuracy = 0.1)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  # Only label segments with sufficient physical height
  mutate(
    count_label = if_else(
      n >= 20 &
        n >= max(decade_total) * 0.035,
      scales::comma(n),
      ""
    )
  )

```

### Stacked count graph

```{r metadata-stacked-counts}

metadata_count_plot <- ggplot(
  metadata_decade,
  aes(
    x = factor(decade),
    y = n,
    fill = metadata_group,
    group = metadata_group
  )
) +

  # Stacked bars

  geom_col(
    aes(text = hover_text),
    position = position_stack(reverse = FALSE),
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.7,
    width = 0.8
  ) +

  # Labels centred within their corresponding segments

  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = count_label
    ),

    position = position_stack(
      vjust = 0.5,
      reverse = FALSE
    ),

    colour = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 2.6,
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = metadata_palette,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Budget and MPAA Availability Across Release Decades",

    subtitle = "Labels are shown only for sufficiently large segments; hover for all counts.",

    x = "Release decade",

    y = "Number of movies",

    fill = "Metadata category"
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 8
    ),

    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "grey75",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.5
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

interactive_plot(metadata_count_plot)

```

## 11.3 100% stacked percentage graph

This graph shows the proportion of each metadata category within each release decade.

Since each bar represents 100% of the movies released during that decade, this allows us to compare metadata availability independently of the total number of movies released.

Only segments occupying at least 7% of their respective bars receive an internal percentage label.

```{r metadata-stacked-percentage}

metadata_percentage_plot <- ggplot(
  metadata_decade,
  aes(
    x = factor(decade),
    y = proportion,
    fill = metadata_group,
    group = metadata_group
  )
) +

  # 100% stacked bars

  geom_col(
    aes(text = hover_text),

    position = position_stack(
      reverse = FALSE
    ),

    colour = "white",

    linewidth = 0.7,

    width = 0.8
  ) +

  # Label only sufficiently large segments

  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = if_else(
        proportion >= 0.07,
        scales::percent(
          proportion,
          accuracy = 1
        ),
        ""
      )
    ),

    position = position_stack(
      vjust = 0.5,
      reverse = FALSE
    ),

    colour = "white",

    fontface = "bold",

    size = 2.6,

    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +

  scale_fill_manual(
    values = metadata_palette,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1),
    limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Proportion of Movies by Metadata Availability",

    subtitle = "Only segments representing at least 7% are labelled.",

    x = "Release decade",

    y = "Percentage of movies",

    fill = "Metadata category"
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 8
    ),

    panel.border = element_rect(
      colour = "grey75",
      fill = NA,
      linewidth = 0.5
    ),

    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

interactive_plot(metadata_percentage_plot)

```

## 11.4 Audience rating by metadata category

The boxplots are calculated using all available movies.

Only the individual points are sampled to reduce interactive rendering workload.

```{r metadata-rating-data}

metadata_rating_data <- movies_analysis %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(rating),
    !is.na(metadata_group)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", title, "</b>",
      "<br>Metadata category: ", metadata_group,
      "<br>Year: ", year,
      "<br>Rating: ", rating,
      "<br>Duration: ", length, " minutes",
      "<br>Budget: ", scales::comma(budget),
      "<br>MPAA: ", mpaa_clean
    )
  )

# Summary statistics using all observations

metadata_rating_summary <- metadata_rating_data %>%
  group_by(metadata_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    Median_rating = median(rating),
    Mean_rating = mean(rating),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Sample individual observations for interactive display

set.seed(2026)

metadata_rating_sample <- sample_by_groups(
  metadata_rating_data,
  group_vars = "metadata_group",
  max_n = 1000
)

```

## 11.5 Metadata category vs rating across release years

This analysis examines how the median audience rating changes over time for each metadata category.

Only year/category combinations containing at least ten movies are included, reducing the influence of groups with very few observations.

```{r metadata-year-rating}

metadata_year_rating <- movies_analysis %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(rating),
    !is.na(metadata_group)
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    year,
    metadata_group
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),

    median_rating = median(rating),

    mean_rating = mean(rating),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    n >= 10
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Year: ", year, "</b>",
      "<br>Metadata category: ", metadata_group,
      "<br>Movies: ", n,
      "<br>Median rating: ",
      round(median_rating, 2),
      "<br>Mean rating: ",
      round(mean_rating, 2)
    )
  )

```

# 12. Final summary

```{r final-summary}

# Safe summary functions to handle entirely missing groups

safe_mean <- function(x) {

  x <- x[is.finite(x)]

  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  mean(x)
}


safe_median <- function(x) {

  x <- x[is.finite(x)]

  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  median(x)
}


# Final comparison between film classifications

final_summary <- movies_analysis %>%

  filter(
    !is.na(film_type)
  ) %>%

  group_by(film_type) %>%

  summarise(

    # Total number of movie records

    Movies = n(),

    # Runtime information

    Movies_with_duration = sum(
      is.finite(length) & length >= 0
    ),

    Median_duration = safe_median(
      length[length >= 0]
    ),

    Mean_duration = safe_mean(
      length[length >= 0]
    ),

    # Audience rating information

    Movies_with_rating = sum(
      is.finite(rating)
    ),

    Median_rating = safe_median(rating),

    Mean_rating = safe_mean(rating),

    # Popularity information

    Movies_with_votes = sum(
      is.finite(votes)
    ),

    Median_votes = safe_median(votes),

    # Audience rating variability

    Movies_with_rating_distribution = sum(
      is.finite(rating_sd_estimated)
    ),

    Mean_estimated_rating_SD = safe_mean(
      rating_sd_estimated
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )


# Display the final summary

clean_table(
  final_summary,
  "Summary comparison of short films and other films",
  digits = 2
)

```


This gives you a more transparent comparison because you can see how many observations contribute to each statistic.

# 13. Conclusions and limitations

The exploratory analysis investigated relationships between movie duration, film classification, genre, audience ratings, popularity and metadata availability.

The analysis addressed the following research questions:

1. Is movie duration associated with average audience ratings?
2. Does this relationship differ between short films and other films?
3. Does the relationship between duration and rating vary across genres?
4. Have movie durations changed historically?
5. Is movie duration associated with audience engagement, as approximated by the number of votes?
6. Are longer movies associated with greater dispersion in audience ratings?
7. Can the distribution of individual audience ratings approximate the reported overall rating?
8. Is metadata availability associated with differences in movie characteristics and audience ratings?

## 13.1 Main methodological considerations

Several limitations should be considered when interpreting the exploratory results.

**Film classification and duration**

The `Short` variable represents a separate film classification indicator and is not defined by a fixed runtime threshold. Consequently, short films should not automatically be interpreted as movies with shorter durations.

**Multiple genre membership**

Movies can belong to multiple content genres simultaneously. Genre-specific analyses may therefore include the same movie in more than one category. The RGB mixtures used to represent genre combinations are a visual encoding and should not be interpreted as a scientific measure of genre similarity.

**Audience ratings and variability**

The reconstructed average rating and standard deviation are approximations because the `r1`–`r10` distribution values are rounded and midpoint-coded.

Furthermore, the reported `rating` and the reconstructed rating distribution originate from the same underlying audience-voting data. Their comparison is therefore a mathematical reconstruction and consistency check rather than an independent validation.

The estimated standard deviation describes the dispersion of individual audience ratings, not the uncertainty or standard error of the reported average.

**Popularity and audience engagement**

The number of votes is used as a proxy for audience engagement and popularity. However, vote counts can also be influenced by factors such as movie age, visibility, distribution and audience size.

Therefore, vote counts should not be interpreted as direct measurements of box-office performance or overall commercial success.

**Budget and MPAA metadata**

Budget information is incomplete, and MPAA classification is not available for every movie. Metadata availability may also vary across release periods.

Consequently, differences between metadata categories should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence that budget or MPAA information causes differences in audience ratings.

## 13.2 Dataset and visualisation limitations

- The dataset ends in 2005 and therefore does not describe contemporary movie production or audience preferences.
- Some visualisations restrict movie runtime to the range of 0–300 minutes to improve interpretability. The final summary in Section 12 uses the complete analytical dataset with valid non-negative runtimes.
- Movies may have missing values for runtime, rating, votes, budget, MPAA classification or reconstructed rating statistics. Individual analyses therefore use different numbers of eligible observations.
- Interactive visualisations use sampled points to improve rendering performance. In Section 10, up to 2,500 movies per film classification are displayed in each interactive plot. In Section 11, up to 1,000 movies per metadata category are displayed in the individual-point layer of the rating boxplot.
- Sampling affects the displayed individual points, not the underlying descriptive statistics, boxplots or fitted regression lines, which are calculated using the complete eligible datasets.

## 13.3 Transition to regression analysis

The exploratory analysis provides an initial understanding of the relationships between movie characteristics and audience ratings.

These observations will guide the selection of explanatory variables, potential interaction terms and model structures in the subsequent regression analysis.

The regression analysis will further investigate which movie characteristics are associated with audience ratings while accounting for the relationships and limitations identified during the exploratory stage.
